title: Chief Engineer
description:
Primary Purpose of Position:

Maintain the integrity of all building systems, provide services to tenants, supervise work of other engineering staff, and operate the building in an efficient manner.

Essential Functions:

Building Operations

  • Ensure the proficient operation of assigned assets, ensuring all systems are maintained in first class condition. Building systems include (and not limited to) HVAC, water treatment program, electrical, lighting, plumbing, elevator, energy management, fire alarm, structural, hardware and key control.

  • Maintain and refine a documented preventative maintenance and service call program for all building systems. Organize and maintain comprehensive record files consisting of operations and maintenance manuals, blueprints (tenant and base building), loss prevention activities, safety training, material safety data and other pertinent documents.

  • Regularly inspect machinery and electrical rooms and all other work areas to ensure good housekeeping and safe working conditions.

  • Maintain daily communications with Regional Property Managers, Director of Engineering and Property Managers on ongoing work and non-routine situations.

  • Responsible for operating within the budget established for designated accounts. Provide input for annual operating budget and anticipated capital expenditures.

  • Review tenant and base building renovation plans and specifications, providing comments relating to design problems or conflicts to existing building systems or structures.

  • Ensure all contracted maintenance, repair or construction activities conform to established building policies and standards. Inform Property Manager of all defective or nonconforming conditions.

  • Provide suggestions and/or plans to improve the operating or energy efficiency of building systems.

  • Maintain all applicable paperwork including purchase order requests and provides appropriate backup for accounting reconciliation. Review and forward completed service request and work order forms per established procedures.

  • Develop and practice emergency operational procedures with staff such as equipment changeover, isolation of electrical and water systems, fire, bomb threat, evacuation, power outages, severe weather, etc.

  • Respond to building emergencies

  • Ensure building standards are maintained as established in the annual property management audit.

Supervisory

  • Effectively manage engineering staff to include activities such as assigning work, providing supervision and direction, conducting employee reviews and facilitating training programs as needed. Ensure employees are qualified, competent, knowledgeable of policies and procedures, and project a positive attitude and appearance.

  • Develop work schedules for assigned staff. Responsible for documentation of timesheets and control of overtime. Obtain approval for non-emergency overtime from the Property Manager.

  • Conduct monthly staff meetings in conjunction with regional and property teams. Each meeting will include a discussion on safety and review of the previous month’s service history that includes the tenant service ticket program as well as other operational or procedural subjects.

General

  • Available for various shifts and to occasionally work extended hours, nights, weekends and holidays to ensure adequate building coverage and perform necessary repairs.

  • Provide exemplary customer service to internal and external customers in a positive and timely manner.

  • Assist in instituting and administering policies and procedures established by Engineering Management.

  • Respond to after hours emergencies such as fire, flooding, severe weather (including snow and ice removal) power outage and other related situations including clean-up activities, if other contracted personnel are not available.

Region/Building Specific Functions:

  • Oversee and support MEP, sustainability, IAQ, general operations of existing assets and support of design, construction and commissioning of new development/acquisitions and related engineering workforce activities.

  • Review tenant and base building renovation plans and specifications, providing comments relating to design problems or conflicts to existing building systems or structures.

  • Manage Angus Anywhere preventative maintenance, loss control and service call programs.

  • Represent Property Management at tenant and base building construction meetings, as necessary.

  • Assist in the technical training and upgrading of skills of more junior personnel.

  • Pursue employee development objectives recommended by the Director of Engineering and/or Regional Property Managers.

  • Assist in the administration of the properties impairment and loss prevention program.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Requirements and Qualifications:

  • High School diploma or equivalent educational certification preferred.

  • Minimum of 10 years of operational experience required with 5 years at a supervisory level or equivalent experience and responsibility preferred.

  • Accredited technical school, military, or college certification in HVAC and/or Operating Engineering Technologies and/or equivalent job related training and experience required.

  • LEED G-Pro preferred.

  • LEED GA preferred.

  • LEED AP O&M preferred.

  • BOMI SMA/RPA Certification or enrollment in program preferred.

  • Universal CFC certification required.

  • Continuing education in field.

  • Advanced computer skills – Building Automation Systems, Microsoft Windows, Excel and Lotus Notes knowledge.

  • Excellent technical and problem solving abilities

  • Ability to work independently.

  • Ability to organize and coordinate work efficiently, set priorities and motivate others.

  • Familiarity with OSHA, NEC, NFC and life safety codes.

Physical Requirements:

  • Regularly required to stand, walk, reach and use arms to perform tasks.

  • Regularly required to talk and hear and occasionally required to taste and smell.

  • Frequently required to sit, stoop, crouch, kneel, crawl, balance and climb stairs and ladders.

  • Regularly required to lift and/or move up to 20 pounds, and occasionally required to lift/move 50+ pounds.

  • Specific vision abilities include close vision, distance vision, color vision and depth perception.

  • Involves movement between departments, buildings, and floors to facilitate work.

Internal and External Contacts:

  • Regularly interfaces with tenants, various Boston Properties staff, vendors, construction professionals and consultants.

Reporting Structure:

  • The Chief Engineer will receive supervision and direction from the Property Manager of the assigned asset. Engineering Management will provide supplemental direction and assistance to the Chief Engineer.

Salary Range:

$102,030 - $145,465. BXP offers a competitive total rewards package including base salary and annual discretionary bonus. The range represents expected base salary; compensation will be determined based on role, skills, experience, qualifications, location, and other job-related factors. Our comprehensive benefits include medical and dental coverage, a retirement savings plan with competitive company match, backup childcare, educational assistance, employee support programs, a generous commuter transit subsidy and more.

BXP is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state, or federal laws, rules, or regulations.

title: Analyst, Institutional Capital Group
description:
Location:

127 Public Square, Cleveland Ohio

ABOUT THE BUSINESS:
KeyBank Real Estate Capital (KBREC) is one of the nation's leading providers of commercial and multifamily real estate finance. KBREC focuses on building long-term relationships with its clients by providing creative financing solutions, acting with a sense of urgency and meeting client objectives. Our broad financing options, integrated platform, and deep industry experience give our clients what they need to meet their short and long-term goals.
The Institutional Real Estate Group (IREG) is affiliated with the broader KeyBank Real Estate Capital platform. Specifically, IREG is focused on the unique capital and banking needs of public and private REITs, real estate operating companies, real estate fund sponsors, and real estate private equity firms. IREG helps institutional real estate entities obtain debt and equity financing in the following ways:

• Corporate Credit Facilities (including Senior Unsecured Revolving Lines of Credit and Term Loans, Senior Secured Lines of Credit, Structurally Subordinate Lines of Credit, and Subscription Lines)
• Syndicated Finance
• Acquisition and Bridge Loans
• Permanent Debt (CMBS, Life Company Placement, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and FHA/HUD)
• Public and Private Bonds (Private Placements, Investment Grade & High Yield bonds)
• Public and Private Equity (IPOs, Common Equity Offerings and Private Placement of Equity)

ABOUT THE JOB:
An Analyst assists senior team members in managing client relationships, reviewing and processing credit requests, and monitoring existing transactions. Analyst support includes, but is not limited to, financial analysis, real estate due diligence, transaction underwriting, credit structuring, portfolio management, creating client-tailored marketing materials, and client interface.

THIS OPPORTUNITY PROVIDES YOU:
• Competitive base salary + discretionary bonus
• Generous benefits – including, 401(k) matching (dollar-for-dollar up to 7%), PTO, a Lifestyle Spending Account in support of employees’ health, well-being and financial wellness, tuition reimbursement and much more.
• Paid on the job training and access to a library of on-demand professional development, training courses and formal enterprise mentoring program.
• Opportunity to be part of a team that is a market-leader in the institutional real estate sector, maintains deep, long-term relationships with its clients, and values teamwork and collaboration.
• Frequent collaboration with internal product partners throughout the organization which broadens the Analyst’s real estate and corporate banking skillset.
• Frequent, timely, and constructive feedback from IREG senior leadership designed to accelerate the Analyst’s career development.
• Tools and mentoring necessary to ultimately become a dynamic member of the Team.


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:
• Work closely with other IREG teammates, including Associates, Relationship Managers and Senior Relationship Managers to build client relationships and provide financing solutions.
• Complete portfolio management, market analysis, and financial underwriting, including writeups(?), for credit transactions.
• Develop detailed knowledge of underwriting parameters and the working relationship between balance sheet lending and off- balance sheet financing options.
• Run and utilize internal modeling to determine risk ratings and return hurdles on all loan approvals.
• Participate as an engaged member of the deal team, effectively and regularly communicating with the IREG team, internal product partners, borrowers, and prospects.
• Work in the office most days is expected, and occasional travel may also be required.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
• Bachelor’s degree
• Strong analytical, organizational, written and verbal communication skills
• Computer literate with proficiency in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
• Demonstrated leadership and teamwork
• Highly motivated, self-directed, and strong work ethic

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• Degree or class work in finance, accounting, commercial real estate, or economics
• Financial modeling coursework or experience
• Relevant internship or prior work experience in commercial real estate or commercial banking

CORE COMPETENCIES:
• Strong communication skills
• Effective time management
• Intellectual curiosity
• Critical thinking
• Team player
• Synthesize/interpret information
• Financial acumen

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

This position is eligible to earn a base salary in the range of $69,000.00 - $105,000.00 annually. Placement within the pay range may differ based upon various factors, including but not limited to skills, experience and geographic location. Compensation for this role also includes eligibility for incentive compensation which may include production, commission, and/or discretionary incentives.

title: Amazon Shopper Insights & Analytics Lead
description:
Clorox is the place that’s committed to growth – for our people and our brands. Guided by our purpose and values, and with people at the center of everything we do, we believe every one of us can make a positive impact on consumers, communities, and teammates. Join our team. #CloroxIsThePlace

Your role at Clorox:

The shopper and retail commerce landscape is shifting faster than ever, blending online and offline behavior, retail media, social commerce, delivery platforms, and AI-driven journeys. Shoppers now discover, evaluate, and buy in atomized moments, not linear funnels.

-This role is ideal for someone who sits at the intersection of analytics + insight + eCommerce, bringing the “art and science” needed to translate complex data into clear, actionable growth outcomes.

-Incremental headcount required to support focus area of eCommerce and Amazon specifically, where regaining share across our portfolio is a priority.

-The Amazon Insight Shopper Lead is a pivotal role that blends eCommerce analytics, shopper insights, and storytelling to unlock growth. You will lead the understanding of the Amazon and eCommerce shopper, synthesizing insights from platforms such as Stackline (Beacon, Atlas), Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC), Circana, Numerator, and be proficient and conducting your own custom research to influence decisions across Sales, Retail Commerce, and BU Marketing.

In this role, you will:

We believe great insights don't end with analysis; they inspire better decisions.

  • Develop forward-looking shopper and category point of views that help Clorox and Amazon anticipate where shoppers, categories, and retail are headed—not just where they've been.
  • Develop a deep understanding of Amazon shoppers by uncovering the behaviors, motivations, missions, and trends that influence purchase decisions across physical and digital commerce.
  • Influence decisions across category strategy, assortment, pricing, innovation, merchandising, digital commerce, and retailer engagement.
  • Integrate shopper research, syndicated data, retailer analytics, digital commerce insights, and market intelligence into clear business recommendations.
  • Identify growth opportunities across categories, brands, shopping missions, and occasions through advanced analytics and consumer understanding.
  • Lead category and shopper learning plans that answer critical business questions and influence commercial strategy.
  • Create compelling, insight-led stories that simplify complex information and inspire action with internal leaders and Amazon partners.
  • Partner closely with Field Sales, Marketing, Consumer Insights, Retail Media, and Data & Analytics teams to solve business challenges.
  • Leverage emerging capabilities, including AI-enabled analytics to accelerate insight generation and improve decision making.
  • Help shape omnichannel strategies by understanding how shoppers move across stores, Amazon.com, pickup, delivery, and digital touchpoints.
  • Directly shaping critical Amazon engagements including (AVNs) and Clorox planning moments of Category Strategy Reviews, Commercial Plan Reviews and Multi-Year planning re – targeting the highest value shoppers, with the right assortment and value offering.

Opportunity to Shape the Future

This is more than an insights and analytics role. You'll help define how Clorox uses shopper understanding to create competitive advantage with Amazon. From AI-enabled analytics to omnichannel commerce and retailer partnerships, you'll influence strategic decisions across some of our biggest brands. Your work won't end with dashboards and analysis it will shape business decisions.

What we look for:

  • 7+ years of experience in Shopper Insights, Consumer Insights, Category Management, Analytics, Customer Insights, or related fields.
  • Amazon experience required, working with a large retailer a plus (e.g. Walmart) and emerging platform experience a plus (e.g. Instacart, Doordash).
  • Strong foundation in both consumer/shopper research and advanced analytics.
  • Experience presenting insights and recommendations directly to retail customers and senior business leaders.
  • Demonstrated success influencing commercial decisions through insight-driven storytelling.
  • Ability to frame business questions, develop learning plans, test hypotheses, and translate findings into action.
  • Deep understanding of consumer and shopper research methodologies, including quantitative, qualitative, syndicated, and behavioral data.
  • Experience developing shopper, category, and path-to-purchase insights that influence commercial strategy.
  • Identify and anticipate emerging shopper behaviors, macro trends, and future growth opportunities before they become obvious in the business.
  • Experience synthesizing multiple data sources into clear, actionable growth-driving recommendations.
  • Strong storytelling skills with the ability to simplify complex analyses for senior leaders and retailer partners.
  • Amazon Marketing Cloud, Stackline, Stackline Omni Shopper Analytics platform required (or demonstrated ability to quickly learn retailer-specific analytics platforms) required.
  • Syndicated data (Circana, NielsenIQ, Numerator) experienced working knowledge and ability.

Workplace type:

Hybrid: This role will ideally be located out of the Pleasanton, CA area, with the ability to be in office 3x per week. Open to top talent that sits out of other Clorox hub locations and remote possibility.

title: Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer
description:
Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer

San Francisco, CA · On-site · Full-time
Compensation: $180K–$280K + equity

About the company

Our client is a seed-stage enterprise-AI company building a platform that captures the operational knowledge generated inside the world’s largest organizations and turns it into a living specification that agentic systems can operate from — working at the intersection of process intelligence and agentic AI. Just months in, they’re already transforming operations for large enterprises, and they’re backed by a top-tier venture firm. This is a chance to be one of the first engineers on a young, clean codebase with real technical ownership.

Founded 2024 · ~10 people · Industry: AI, Enterprise, B2B

The role

You’ll be a core early engineering hire building a production platform end-to-end. You’ll write idiomatic Go, ship a modern React frontend, and design systems that put LLMs to work in production — making architectural calls, living with the results, and iterating based on how things perform in the real world and what customers tell you.

What you’ll be doing

  • Own features end-to-end, from design through deployment and monitoring
  • Build and operate reliable backend systems in Go and Python
  • Build and maintain a modern React/TypeScript frontend
  • Design and ship production systems that integrate LLMs (orchestration, tool calling, context management, evals)
  • Work directly with the founding team and iterate on features from direct customer feedback

Tech stack: Go, Python, PostgreSQL, Redis, React 19 + TypeScript, GCP, Terraform, Docker, Datadog, GitHub

Requirements

  • 5–10 years of full-stack software engineering experience, with real strength in a typed language (Go preferred), Python, and React/TypeScript
  • A track record of shipping production services with concrete, verifiable contributions across the stack and sustained ownership of meaningful systems
  • Hands-on experience building production systems that integrate with LLMs (real systems, not just prototypes), with a working grasp of patterns like orchestration, tool calling, context management, and evals
  • Solid PostgreSQL depth — schema design, migrations, and production operations
  • Proven experience iterating on features from direct customer feedback, with strong written and verbal communication
  • A pragmatic engineering mindset (knowing when to refactor vs. ship, build vs. buy) and a track record of leading larger, high-impact projects
  • A genuine understanding of what it takes to be a founding engineer in an early-stage environment
  • A BS or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (a top-30 CS program is a plus, especially earlier in your career)
  • Able to work on-site 5 days a week in San Francisco

Nice to haves

  • Early-stage startup experience, or a mix of big-tech and startup backgrounds
  • Infrastructure-as-Code experience (Terraform, GCP, Docker)

Why join

  • Get in early on a category-defining product at the intersection of process intelligence and agentic AI
  • Real technical ownership across the full stack in a young, clean codebase
  • Work directly with a founding team that’s already in market with large enterprises
  • Senior compensation plus meaningful early-stage equity

Details

  • Location: San Francisco, CA
  • Work policy: On-site, 5 days/week
  • Compensation: $180K–$280K + equity
  • Visa sponsorship: Open to transfers (e.g. STEM OPT, H-1B transfer, TN)
  • Employment type: Full-time

title: Internship Position (Digital Signoff Group)
description:
At Cadence, we hire and develop leaders and innovators who want to make an impact on the world of technology.

About Cadence

Cadence is a global technology company (CDNS) and a key player in the design and production of semiconductor chips worldwide. From 5G mobile phones to Mars rovers and satellites, our products are used by the world’s leading technology companies to design world-class electronic systems. As semiconductor technology continues to evolve, our software must continuously advance to meet the ever-changing needs of our customers.

Cadence Ireland is entering an exciting phase of growth with the creation of a new R&D Centre of Excellence. Our goal is to make a significant contribution to advancing the state of the art and delivering the next generation of Electronic Design Automation (EDA) solutions to major semiconductor companies worldwide.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly motivated Product Engineering (PE) Intern to join the Pegasus physical verification team. Pegasus is Cadence’s next-generation physical verification platform used by semiconductor foundries and chip design companies to perform critical signoff verification tasks, including Design Rule Checking (DRC), Layout Versus Schematic (LVS), Fill, Pattern Matching, and advanced manufacturing verification.

As a Product Engineering Intern, you will work closely with Product Engineers, R&D teams, and leading semiconductor customers to help develop, validate, and deploy cutting-edge verification solutions. This role provides hands-on exposure to advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies and industry-leading EDA software.

Responsibilities

  • Assist in testing and validating Pegasus physical verification flows and new product features.
  • Develop and execute verification test cases to ensure product quality and robustness.
  • Analyse verification results, investigate issues, and help reproduce customer-reported problems.
  • Work with Product Engineering and R&D teams to debug and resolve technical issues.
  • Support the qualification of new semiconductor process technologies and design rules.
  • Create automation scripts and tools to improve engineering productivity and test coverage.
  • Prepare technical documentation, reports, and presentations summarising findings and recommendations.
  • Collaborate with global teams across Europe, Asia, and North America on customer and technology initiatives.

Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Basic Programming or scripting experience (Python, Shell, Perl, or similar) is desirable.
  • Knowledge of semiconductor design, IC layout, or EDA tools.
  • Familiarity with Linux/Unix environments is an advantage.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and willingness to learn new technologies.

What You Will Gain

  • Exposure to state-of-the-art semiconductor design and verification technologies.
  • Experience working on real-world projects used by leading semiconductor companies.
  • Mentorship from experienced Product Engineering and R&D professionals.
  • Opportunities to contribute to innovative solutions in advanced process nodes and next-generation chip design.
  • Experience in a collaborative, multicultural engineering environment with global impact.

We’re doing work that matters. Help us solve what others can’t.

title: Electronics Technician III
description:
Crane Aerospace and Electronics has an exciting opportunity for an Electronics Technician III at our Chandler, AZ location.

About Crane:

Crane Aerospace & Electronics supplies critical systems and components to the aerospace and defense markets. You’ll find Crane Aerospace & Electronics in some of the toughest environments: from engines to landing gear; from satellites to medical implants and from missiles to unmanned aerial systems (UAS).

From supplying microwave products for GPS satellites to integrated assemblies for the latest innovative defense platforms, come join an industry-leading aerospace & defense manufacturer based in beautiful, sunny Chandler, Arizona. You’ll join a first-class, dynamic organization steeped in rich culture and an established track record of delivering customers premier, quality products. You’ll work shoulder-to-shoulder with prime OEMs and help us develop state-of-the art solutions – all in a family-first community with top-rated schools and an abundance of recreational activities. Start the next chapter of your career with Crane Aerospace & Electronics!

Job Summary:

The Electronics Technician III works under limited direction/supervision and is responsible to test, troubleshoot, repair, and modify production of electronic or mechanical products, parts, equipment and systems, such as computer equipment, instrumentation, digital / analog, electronic products, test equipment, electro-mechanical products, applying principles and theories of electronics, electrical circuitry, and electronic testing

Essential Functions:

  • Read and interpret blueprints, wiring diagrams, schematics, work orders, and test procedures to perform testing on electronic and mechanical units using engineering documentation and theory.

  • Perform automated and manual testing using equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, signal generators, ICT, flying probe, vibe, burn‑in, thermal cycle systems, and other special‑purpose testers; maintain system logs and documentation.

  • Calibrate, adjust, and troubleshoot units down to the component level using electrical and mechanical calculations (voltage, resistance, impedance, flow, mechanical dimensions, etc.).

  • Create detailed non‑conformance reports, documenting failures and initial root‑cause findings, and collaborate with design/test engineering to resolve production problems.

  • Support CBS initiatives (5S, KPIs, Standard Work, problem solving), follow OSHA and company safety practices, and perform limited soldering/microscope work as needed.

  • Test higher‑complexity units under limited supervision and provide troubleshooting support across programs.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Experience: 3-5 years of experience in a related field, or equivalent educational experience

  • Knowledge: Extensive knowledge of methods and procedure in troubleshooting, circuitry or mechanical characteristics as related to area of assignment and ability to devise and adapt; Familiarity with product flow through a manufacturing or repair environment; Working knowledge of computer systems

  • Skills: Good oral expression and comprehension (communicate through speech so others will understand and listen to and understand information and ideas presented through speech); Good written expression and comprehension (communicate in English through writing so others will understand and read and understand information and ideas presented in English through writing)

  • Abilities: Ability to learn new test software and equipment and to identify abnormal conditions in equipment and product; Manual and finger dexterity (ability to quickly move your hand, your hand together with your arm, or your two hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects); Ability to make precisely coordinated movements; Ability to work in multiple software systems, including time enter, data enter, on-line training PDM and MRP systems

  • Education/Certification: AA degree in Electronic or Mechanical Technology, or equivalent knowledge through experience or other recognized educational institution.

  • Eligibility Requirement: This position may require access to Controlled Data or Information. Where the position requires such access only US Persons will be considered. As a US Department of Defense contractor, we are bound by International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Applicants selected could be subject to a Government security investigation and must meet the eligibility requirements for access to classified information.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Knowledge of raw materials, production processes, quality control, costs, and other techniques for maximizing the effective manufacture and distribution of goods

  • Knowledge of practical application of engineering electronics, science, and technology including applying principles, techniques, procedures, and equipment to the design and production of various goods and services

  • Knowledge of circuit boards, processors, chips, electronic equipment, and computer hardware and software, including applications and programming

Working Conditions:

  • Working conditions are normal for a manufacturing environment

  • Manufacturing operations may require the use of safety equipment to include but not limited to: eye safety glasses, gowning, masks, hearing protectors, heel/wrist straps and any other required PPE

  • May be exposed to unusual environmental conditions such as loud noises, cold temperatures, confined spaces, dust or fumes

  • May require occasional travel to support customer

Standing: 20% *percentage is approximate and may vary depending on work task Sitting: 80% *percentage is approximate and may vary depending on work task Lifting (in pounds): up to 35 pounds

Pushing (in pounds): up to 100 pounds

Mental/Visual: use of microscope and computer

Workspace: clean bench

Top Benefits:

  • As a team member at Crane Aerospace and Electronics, you’ll enjoy:

  • Benefits: Health care, dental, vision, life and disability insurance starting the first day of the month

  • Time Off: 15 days of paid time off that start accruing your first day at Crane and 12 paid holidays per year.

  • 401k Retirement Plan: 401k plan with company match

  • Education Reimbursement: eligible after 6 months of employment

​

You can see a list of our benefits at https://www.craneae.com/company/careers or visit our website at www.CraneAE.com for more information on our company and great opportunities.

We are committed to operational excellence and world class processes. We employ Lean manufacturing techniques to optimize manufacturing efficiency and accuracy on all product lines. Our products are known for their technical strength, proven reliability and overall value.

title: ASSOCIATE DIRECTOR, DEVELOPMENT

The Associate Director, Development is a frontline fundraising professional responsible for managing a portfolio of alumni, parents, and friends of Ithaca College with the capacity and inclination to make leadership annual gifts, with a primary focus on the Blue & Gold Giving Society. The position manages prospects through discovery, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship and works collaboratively with colleagues, faculty, and senior leadership to strengthen donor relationships and advance leadership annual giving. This position may be performed remotely for individuals residing within the assigned geographic territory (Metro NYC). Individuals residing outside the assigned territory must be within reasonable commuting distance of Ithaca College.

Supervision:

Reports to: Senior Director, Development
Supervises: None

Key Responsibilities:

Prospect Management

  • Manage a portfolio of leadership annual giving prospects, including alumni, parents, and friends, through discovery, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.

Fundraising

description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. Torch Technologies is seeking a motivated Software Developer to support the development, integration, testing, and analysis of missile defense models and simulations. The ideal candidate will possess strong software-development experience and proficiency in Java, C++, Git, and Docker container technologies. This individual will work closely with engineers and technical personnel to develop and maintain modeling and simulation infrastructure; integrate missile defense component models into larger simulation environments; and support the verification, validation, analysis, and delivery of reliable simulation products. The ideal candidate will possess excellent communication skills, both oral and written, and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.

Some of the primary responsibilities will include:

  • Modeling & Simulation Software Development: Design, develop, modify, and maintain software applications, component models, and simulation services supporting missile defense modeling and simulation activities.
  • M&S Infrastructure Development: Develop, configure, and maintain modeling and simulation infrastructure, development environments, interfaces, tools, and supporting services required to execute missile defense simulations.
  • Component Model Integration: Integrate missile defense component models into larger simulation environments; develop and maintain software interfaces; and resolve interoperability, data-exchange, and execution issues.
  • Software Testing & Analysis: Develop and execute unit, integration, regression, and system-level tests to verify software functionality, model behavior, interface compatibility, and simulation performance.
  • Technical Troubleshooting: Investigate, diagnose, document, and resolve complex software, model, interface, build, deployment, and runtime issues.
  • Containerization & Deployment: Use Docker containers to package, configure, deploy, and maintain software applications and modeling and simulation environments.
  • Configuration Management: Use Git and established configuration-management processes to manage source code, maintain version history, support collaborative development, and control software releases.
  • Engineering Team Collaboration: Work closely with engineers, analysts, and other technical personnel to define software requirements, implement technical solutions, analyze simulation results, and deliver customer-required products.

Job Requirements:

  • US Citizenship.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • 2 plus years applicable software design engineering experience.
  • Experience developing software using Java and C++.
  • Experience developing, integrating, testing, and analyzing software applications, component models, or simulations.
  • Proficiency using Git for source-code version control, collaborative development, branch management, and software configuration management.
  • Experience using Docker containers to package, deploy, configure, or maintain software applications and development or simulation environments.
  • Ability to develop and maintain software interfaces and integrate component-level software into larger systems or simulation environments.
  • Ability to troubleshoot and resolve software-development, integration, test, deployment, and performance issues.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively within a diverse team environment and collaborate with engineers, analysts, and technical support personnel.
  • Must have an active security clearance or the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

Preferred Attributes:

  • Proficiency developing or maintaining software using Ada and Fortran.
  • Experience supporting missile defense modeling and simulation software-development activities.
  • Previous software-development experience supporting missile defense command-and-control systems.
  • Experience with the Integrated Battle Command System (IBCS), Patriot, or related air and missile defense systems.
  • Experience working in classified, secure, or government customer environments.
  • Experience with automated testing, continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, or other modern software-development practices.

title: Associate Director, Communications - Internal Communications
description:
Our Communications and Media Relations team is essential for shaping the Firm’s public image and managing its interactions with the media. Our team crafts and disseminates press releases, media statements and other communications to highlight the Firm’s achievements, legal victories and superb insights. We build and maintain relationships with journalists and media outlets to secure positive coverage and handle media inquiries with professionalism and accuracy. The team also oversees internal communications, ensuring that employees are informed about key initiatives and developments. Additionally, we manage the Firm’s social media presence, create engaging content and monitor public perception to proactively address any potential issues. Through strategic communication efforts, our team ensures that the Firm’s reputation remains strong and its messaging consistent across all platforms.

The Associate Director, Executive Communications will be a senior member of the Firm’s Internal Communications team, with primary responsibility for shaping and helping to execute the communications platform of the Chair of a global powerhouse law firm.

Operating as both a strategic adviser and a hands-on content leader, the Associate Director will help define the themes, narratives and messages that underpin the Chair’s internal and external communications. The role will translate the Firm’s strategy, commercial priorities and culture into clear, compelling content for partners, employees, clients and other external stakeholders.

The Associate Director will work closely with the Global Head of Communications, the Chair, firm leadership, and leadership across Marketing and Business Development. The successful candidate will be an exceptional writer and strategic thinker who can navigate a complex, global law firms, provide confident counsel at the most senior levels, and deliver high-quality work with pace, discretion and sound judgment.

The roles and responsibilities of this job include:

  • Serve as a trusted communications adviser and thought partner to the Chair, helping to shape her leadership voice, key messages and overarching communications platform.

  • Develop and execute communications strategies that advance the Chair’s priorities and reinforce the Firm’s strategy and market positioning.

  • Lead the development of executive communications, including speeches, presentations, leadership messages, talking points, briefing materials, video scripts and other high-profile content.

  • Help to shape the content, narrative and structure of major partner convenings (e.g. Global Partner Meetings), firm meetings, global town halls, etc.

  • Translate complex issues and strategic priorities into clear, persuasive and audience-relevant communications.

  • Work closely with colleagues across Internal Communications, External Communications, Content Strategy and Integrated Marketing to ensure the Chair’s communications are coordinated, consistent and mutually reinforcing.

  • Provide strategic and editorial guidance to communications colleagues and firm colleagues contributing to leadership content and Firmwide initiatives.

  • Anticipate emerging communications needs and manage multiple high-profile, time-sensitive priorities with sound judgment and discretion.

  • Help lead the Communications function’s adoption and integration of AI, identifying practical opportunities to improve the quality, speed and efficiency of its work while maintaining appropriate standards, governance and oversight.

  • Contribute to the strategic direction, continued development and effectiveness of the Internal Communications team.

The qualifications for this role are:

  • Significant experience in executive, corporate or internal communications, ideally within a global professional-services firm or another complex, matrixed organization.

  • Demonstrated experience advising a Chair, CEO or other senior executive and developing communications in support of an executive leadership platform.

  • Exceptional writing, editing and storytelling skills, with the ability to capture an executive’s authentic voice and communicate complex subjects clearly and compellingly.

  • Strong strategic judgment and the ability to connect communications activity to broader business and reputational priorities.

  • Experience developing speeches, presentations and content for high-profile leadership events and engagements.

  • Proven ability to build credibility and trusted relationships with senior leaders and stakeholders across multiple functions and geographies.

  • Ability to operate effectively at both the strategic and executional levels, moving comfortably from advising senior leaders to drafting and refining detailed content.

  • Strong organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver consistently high-quality work under tight deadlines.

  • High degree of discretion, maturity and confidence when handling sensitive or confidential matters.

  • A collaborative, pragmatic and solutions-oriented approach.

  • Familiarity with AI-enabled communications tools and a strong interest in applying emerging technology responsibly to improve communications outcomes.

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, English, marketing or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

The Admissions and Recruiting Director will play a crucial role in increasing enrollment for both the 3-Year MD and 6-Year BS/MD programs, shaping Arkansas’s future physicians through strategic partnerships and strong student support. Join us in inspiring the next generation of medical professionals and advancing our mission of excellence in education and community service. If you are a strategic leader who leverages analytics, partnerships, and technology to promote student success and institutional growth, we invite you to apply!

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities:

  • In-depth knowledge of medical education programs and clinical partnerships
  • Excellent oral and written communication; strong public speaking and presentation skills
  • Relationship-building with diverse stakeholders (students, families, premedical advisors, colleges, community partners)

  • Project management and ability to manage multiple initiatives concurrently
  • Training in curriculum administration, scheduling, and instructional support
  • Credentialing processes and coordination with clinical sites
  • Data-informed decision-making; ability to analyze enrollment trends and program outcomes
  • Budget awareness and resource management
  • Proficiency with MS Office; experience with CRM/Admissions systems; familiarity with Workday or other ERP systems is a plus
  • Valid driver’s license and willingness to travel regionally

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in education, administration, healthcare, or related field
  • Ten (10)+ years of experience coordinating education programs, administration, project/program management, healthcare, or related field


Additional Information:

Key Responsibilities:

Recruitment/Admissions Management

  • Collaborate on recruitment activities for traditional and accelerated medical program tracks at the Northwest campus College of Medicine
  • Manage the scheduling system for prospective students to arrange informational meetings and campus tours
  • Meet with prospective students to provide information about UAMS College of Medicine
  • Support recruitment and admissions by coordinating and participating in applicant interviews for all programs
  • Schedule and implement recruitment visits/events at colleges and universities in the region

  • Coordinate student orientation, longitudinal clinic schedules, and summer clerkship placements
  • Manage student placements and onboarding at affiliated community hospitals and clinical sites, ensuring credentialing and external partner communication
  • Maintain program grade books and coordinate course/program evaluations
  • Provide teaching and academic program support for the curriculum, including classroom scheduling, technology coordination, review of instructional materials, and management of student requests
  • Schedule regular meetings with faculty and students for program overview and adaptation

6-Year BS/MD Program Management

  • Assist in the design, implementation, and management of the 6-Year MD curriculum in collaboration with internal departments and the University of Arkansas
  • Manage daily operations, logistics, and timelines to ensure successful program delivery
  • Coordinate student orientation, onboarding, clinical rotations, didactic sessions, and simulations
  • Provide academic and instructional support, including scheduling, technology coordination, teaching materials, and student requests
  • Coordinate student placements, onboarding, and credentialing at affiliated clinical sites; maintain external partner communications
  • Monitor quality of clinical and academic experiences; track attendance, evaluations, performance, and academic progress
  • Serve as primary liaison among students, faculty, administration, and clinical partners; address student concerns and facilitate effective communication

title: K-12 Partnership Coordinator
description:
Job Description

Montgomery College, Rockville Campus, is accepting applications for a Casual Temporary, K-12 Partnership Coordinator. This is a non-bargaining, non-exempt, temporary position. Non-exempt positions are no eligible to work a secondary job at Montgomery College. Montgomery College promotes and creates a working and learning environment rooted in the basic tenets of fairness, belonging and inclusiveness.

The K-12 Partnership Coordinator will extend beyond the coordination of individual programs and events to supporting the development, implementation, and sustainability of a coordinated collegewide approach to K–12 engagement in an effort to directly advance the College’s Strategic Plan (SPOL) and Academic Master Plan (AMP) priorities.

This is a temporary position without benefits funded through June 30, 2027. Employment continuation beyond this period is contingent on need and funding.

Duties include but are not limited to:

  • Lead the planning, coordination, and implementation of the collegewide MC Experience across multiple campuses in alignment with the Strategic Plan and Academic Master Plan.
  • Coordinate with MCPS, faculty, academic leadership, Facilities, IT, Public Safety, Compliance, catering, and other College partners to manage program logistics and requirements.
  • Develop event schedules, secure campus spaces, coordinate transportation and school participation, and manage student group assignments and campus activities.
  • Recruit, coordinate, and train faculty presenters, student group leaders, volunteers, and faculty assistants.
  • Manage the faculty proposal process, including solicitation, review, selection, notification, and coordination of resources for hands-on academic experiences.
  • Ensure compliance with Youth Protection requirements, chaperone ratios, accessibility needs, and other College and MCPS protocols.
  • Coordinate event communications, materials, signage, meals, photography, and day-of operations across campuses.
  • Develop contingency plans and make real-time operational adjustments related to weather, school delays, attendance, and other circumstances.
  • Develop and administer program evaluations, facilitate post-event reviews, and report outcomes, challenges, and recommendations to College leadership.
  • Develop and implement expanded curriculum-focused middle school campus experiences that connect 7th- and 8th-grade students with MC academic programs, faculty, career pathways, and student ambassadors.
  • Lead the planning, coordination, and execution of the annual Dual Enrollment Recognition Ceremony in partnership with MCPS and College stakeholders.
  • Coordinate with senior leadership, Special Events, MCTV, Facilities, Public Safety, Advancement, catering, accessibility services, and external vendors.
  • Convene and lead the ceremony planning committee and maintain ongoing communication with College and MCPS partners.
  • Develop the ceremony program, script, timeline, floor plan, student seating, platform party arrangements, and VIP protocols.
  • Coordinate identification and verification of eligible Dual Enrollment students completing an MC degree or earning 45 or more college credits.
  • Manage student communications, RSVPs, recognition materials, student speakers, performers, and ceremony participation requirements.
  • Coordinate participation of College and MCPS senior leadership, Board of Trustees and Board of Education members, and other dignitaries.
  • Manage event logistics, including catering, photography, audiovisual production, accessibility services, security, facilities, signage, parking, and contracted services.
  • Lead ceremony rehearsals, day-of operations, and the post-ceremony reception, addressing operational issues as needed.
  • Conduct post-event assessment with MC, MCPS, and event partners and document successes, challenges, and recommendations for future ceremonies.
  • Coordinate the planning and implementation of curriculum-focused campus visits for middle school students across Montgomery College campuses.
  • Collaborate with MCPS schools, MC faculty, academic departments, and campus partners to coordinate visit schedules, logistics, and student participation.
  • Identify and coordinate faculty-led, hands-on academic experiences aligned with students’ interests and College programs and career pathways.
  • Coordinate student group leaders, campus tours, classroom space, transportation logistics, and other operational needs.
  • Develop standardized schedules, communications, materials, and procedures to support a consistent and scalable campus visit model.
  • Collect and evaluate student and stakeholder feedback to assess program effectiveness and inform future programming.
  • Support alignment of the initiative with Strategic Plan Outcome 1 and the College’s broader K–12 pathway and early engagement efforts.
  • Lead a collegewide inventory of programs, events, and engagement opportunities serving students in Grades 6–8.
  • Establish and maintain a centralized repository of middle school programs and activities offered across academic departments, campuses, and College offices.
  • Develop and maintain an outreach tracking system to coordinate engagement efforts, identify gaps and reduce duplication across the College.
  • Collaborate with College departments to ensure program information is current, accurate, and effectively promoted.
  • Develop and implement a comprehensive marketing and awareness plan to increase visibility of Montgomery College opportunities among middle school students and families.
  • Coordinate development and maintenance of a centralized middle school webpage highlighting programs, events, academic experiences, and pathways.
  • Develop and coordinate Middle School Prep-Talk to introduce students and families to MC programs, college preparation, and future academic pathways.
  • Coordinate outreach and promotion with MCPS, community organizations, families, and other partners to broaden participation and awareness.
  • Monitor participation and outreach data to identify underserved schools, communities, and student populations and inform future engagement strategies.
  • Support alignment of Grades 6–8 outreach and engagement activities with Strategic Plan Outcome 1, the Academic Master Plan, and the College’s broader K–12 pathway strategy.

Required Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in education, public administration, or a related field.
  • At least three years of progressively responsible experience in program coordination, outreach, or academic initiatives (or an equivalent combination of education and experience).
  • Experience working in higher education or with K-12 partnerships.
  • Familiarity with dual enrollment, or other academic pathways programs.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple projects with competing priorities.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to draft reports, memos, and presentations.
  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with diverse internal and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, data management tools, and presentation software.
  • High level of discretion, initiative, and attention to detail.

Hiring Rage: $60.00 per hour

For degrees earned outside of the U.S., a copy of your education equivalency, conducted by a nationally recognized evaluation service, must be included in your application.

As a condition of employment, the following are required at the time of hire:

  • Successful completion of a background check and degree verification (if applicable).

If a reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact Human Resources and Strategic Talent Management at 240-567-5353 or HRSTM@montgomerycollege.edu. We require at least two weeks advance notice to enable us to provide the requested accommodation.

Montgomery College is an equal opportunity employer committed to promoting and fostering diversity among its student body, faculty, and staff.

Montgomery College is a tobacco-free and smoke-free workplace.

Wednesday, September 16, 2026

title: Laboratory Assistant
description:
This Laboratory Assistant is responsible for a wide range of duties that include coordinating the calibration of test equipment, purchasing supplies, shipping, logging test samples, and providing facility support necessary for efficient site and laboratory operations. The role also supports asset management, inventory control, document and record maintenance, visitor and vendor coordination, laboratory testing support, and compliance with safety and quality requirements. The Laboratory Assistant serves as a key operational resource to ensure the effective functioning of laboratory, facility, and administrative processes.

• Coordinates the site calibration program by generating and distributing calibration-due reports, tracking equipment status, creating work orders and shipping documentation, arranging outside or onsite calibration, reviewing returned equipment and certificates, updating asset records, recording costs, and routing equipment back to the responsible department.

• Maintains asset records and traceability documentation for calibration and laboratory equipment, including equipment locations, service history, certificates, and status updates within designated business systems.

• Coordinates purchasing activities in accordance with global sourcing and purchasing policies, including supplier verification and onboarding, purchase requisitions and purchase orders, cost allocation, blanket purchase orders, invoice tracking, receiving, payment follow-up, and year-end purchase order renewal.

• Monitors and replenishes laboratory, testing, critical consumable, shipping, office, breakroom, building, personal protective equipment, first aid, and battery supplies. Maintains required certificates, conditioning records, inventories, and other traceability documentation for critical consumables.

• Maintains records for recurring invoices and site expenses, resolves purchase order and invoice discrepancies, and supports purchasing and laboratory equipment audits by organizing required documentation.

• Coordinates shipping and receiving activities for laboratory samples, equipment, and calibration items. Reviews shipping instructions, prepares packages and packing slips, submits shipping requests, records tracking and cost information, and confirms receipt and condition of returned items.

• Builds and/or adapts basic setups and test equipment for the performance of tests. Performs tests using general laboratory equipment and provides routine care of designated test equipment and work areas.

• Follows defined test plans and data sheets. Evaluates test performance and sample operation, records observed or calculated data, and explains test results.

• Reads and interprets test results, measuring instruments, and prepares accurate, complete and concise reports to reflect significant facts. Prepares charts, graphs, and reports using spreadsheets and documents to communicate results.

• Operates designated laboratory equipment and tools as directed. Receives instructions from and reports data to engineers and other laboratory staff, while developing working knowledge of job methods, instrumentation, and systems.

• Coordinates visitor, contractor, and vendor access activities in accordance with site safety, security, and visitor management procedures.

• Self-motivated to identify tasks that need to be completed and bring them to completion.

• Communicates effectively with internal customers, suppliers, service providers, calibration vendors, and other external contacts to coordinate work and resolve routine issues.

• Participates in environmental, health, and safety (EHS) activities, inspections, corrective actions, and compliance initiatives to support a safe working environment.

• Integrates continuous improvement concepts and techniques into all aspects of the job.

• Reads and follows the Underwriters Laboratories Code of Conduct and all applicable physical and digital security practices.

• Performs other duties as directed.

•Higher Secondary Education. Effective communication skills and ability to interact with customers.

• Desire to work in a team-oriented environment.

• Ability to use Microsoft Office suite is a must, particularly Outlook, Excel, and Word.

• Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with customers, suppliers, service providers, and coworkers.

• Ability to maintain accurate records, organize multiple priorities, follow established procedures, and handle purchasing, calibration, shipping, and safety documentation.

• Ability to work independently, prioritize multiple responsibilities, and manage deadlines with minimal supervision.

• Experience supporting purchasing, inventory management, shipping/receiving, laboratory operations, facilities coordination, or administrative functions preferred.

• Demonstrated problem-solving skills and the ability to coordinate activities across multiple departments, vendors, and service providers.

• Familiarity with laboratory safety practices, personal protective equipment (PPE), and compliance requirements preferred.

• Ability to safely handle routine laboratory equipment, packages, supplies, and materials in accordance with site procedures.

• Possess an attention to detail.

• Must be able to lift 40 pounds unassisted.

Total Rewards: We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. The estimated salary range for this position is $37,000- $40,000 and is based on multiple factors, including job-related knowledge/skills, experience, geographical location, as well as other factors. This position is eligible for annual bonus compensation with a target payout of 5% of the base salary. This position also provides health benefits such as medical, dental and vision; wellness benefits such as mental and financial health; and retirement savings (401K) commensurate with the standard rewards offered in each individual location or country. We also provide full-time employees with paid time off including vacation (15 days), holiday and personal days (totaling 12 days), and sick time off (72 hours).

title: Access Excellence Senior Director
description:
HealthPartners is hiring a Access Excellence Senior Director. This leader provides strategic leadership and oversight for enterprise access infrastructure, including referral and order lifecycle management, scheduling decision-support tools, provider and clinician directory governance, access analytics, and enabling technologies. This role is accountable for the design, optimization, and continuous improvement of workflows that support patient access across internal, external, self-scheduling, hospital discharge, and Care Everywhere referral pathways. The position serves as the enterprise owner of scheduling decision trees, templates, clinician profiles, and provider finder tools, ensuring accurate, standardized, and consumer-friendly access experiences across all channels. Working closely with operational, clinical, digital, analytics, and information technology teams, the role drives data-informed improvements and oversees access-related technology capabilities, including Epic, Cisco/cloud telephony platforms, digital scheduling tools, and emerging AI-enabled solutions. This position develops and executes strategies that improve access, streamline operations, enhance patient experience, and support organizational growth and performance objectives.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Education, Experience or Equivalent Combination:
    • Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience.
    • Seven (7) or more years of formal people leadership experience within a complex, matrixed healthcare environment.
    • Experience working within a health system utilizing Epic.
    • Previous healthcare operations experience.
  • Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
    • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence and build relationships across all levels of the organization.
    • Ability to lead effectively through ambiguity, change, and shifting priorities in a dynamic environment.
    • Strong people leadership capabilities, including employee engagement, coaching, mentoring, and driving accountability for results.
    • Demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment while managing complex information and competing priorities.
    • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and Epic, with the ability to leverage technology to support operational excellence.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Education, Experience or Equivalent Combination:
    • Master’s degree in a related field.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES:

  1. (30%) - Operational Leadership:
    1. Provide strategic and operational leadership for enterprise access infrastructure, including referral and order lifecycle management, scheduling support tools, provider directory governance, and access-related technologies.
    2. Oversee the design, implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of workflows supporting internal, external, self-scheduling, hospital discharge, and Care Everywhere referral pathways.
    3. Ensure operational excellence through process standardization, workflow optimization, and effective management of enterprise access capabilities. (30%) – Strategic Direction and Scheduling Excellence:
  2. (30%) – Strategic Direction and Access Optimization:
    1. Establish the vision, strategy, and governance for enterprise access enablement functions, aligning priorities with organizational access, growth, and patient experience objectives.
    2. Serve as the enterprise owner of scheduling decision trees, scheduling templates, clinician profiles, and provider finder tools, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and ongoing optimization.
    3. Lead strategic initiatives that improve access performance, referral conversion, scheduling effectiveness, and consumer navigation across all access channels. (10%) – Financial and Resource Management:
  3. (20%) – Collaboration, Analytics, and Stakeholder Engagement:
    1. Partner with clinical, operational, digital, and enterprise leaders to develop and implement access strategies that improve patient navigation and operational outcomes.
    2. Provide leadership for access-related data, reporting, and analytics, including the development, maintenance, and publication of key performance metrics and actionable insights.
    3. Serve as a strategic liaison between operations and technology teams to ensure alignment of access goals, workflows, and system capabilities.
  4. (10%) – Technology and Resource Management:
    1. Provide oversight and prioritization of access-related technology investments and capabilities, including Epic, Cisco and cloud telephony platforms, digital scheduling tools, and AI-enabled solutions.
    2. Collaborate with Information Technology and digital teams to evaluate, implement, and optimize technologies that support access, efficiency, and patient experience goals.
    3. Ensure effective stewardship of resources and technology solutions to maximize organizational value and performance.
  5. (10%) – Leadership and Team Development:
    1. Lead and develop high-performing teams through effective talent management, performance oversight, succession planning, and employee engagement.
    2. Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement while ensuring alignment with organizational values and strategic priorities.
    3. Build partnerships across operational, clinical, digital, analytics, and technology functions to advance enterprise access objectives.
  6. Performs other duties as assigned.

title: Patient Transport 32h Evenings (Every other weekend)
description:
Scheduled Weekly Hours: 32

-

Under the supervision of the EVS, Patient Transport and Linen Services Director, the Transportation Aide provides safe and efficient patient and equipment transport services within the hospital. This role is responsible for moving patients, equipment, and materials between departments while ensuring patient safety, comfort, and dignity. The Transportation Aide supports hospital operations by facilitating timely and organized movement, assisting clinical staff as needed, and maintaining compliance with hospital safety and infection control policies.

Education/Training:

  • High school graduate or equivalent preferred

Licenses/Certification:

• N/A

Required Qualifications and Skills:

  • Ability to safely transport patients, staff, and equipment throughout the hospital.
  • Confirmed understanding and adherence to hospital policies, safety procedures and infection control practices.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to follow written and verbal instructions accurately.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.
  • Reliable and punctual, while consistently maintaining a professional demeanor.
  • Ability to read, write and comprehend basic medical terminology
  • Ability to utilize positive interpersonal skills when interacting with patients and taking into consideration cultural background, linguistic skills and age of customers.

Preferred Qualifications and Skills:

  • Previous experience in a hospital, healthcare, or patient transport setting.
  • Basic Life Support (BLS) certification preferred
  • Ability to assist patients with mobility limitations safely and compassionately.
  • Knowledge of hospital layout, departments, and workflow processes
  • Experience using hospital communication systems (transport software, radios, phones, or pagers)
  • Experience interacting with diverse patient populations in a professional manner.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Safely transport patients between departments, including to and from patient rooms, diagnostic testing areas, Emergency Department, hospital-based clinics, and discharge areas.
  • Facilitate transport of equipment, supplies, and medical records as needed to support clinical and operational workflow.
  • Appropriately identify patients prior to actual transport to ensure two positive identifiers in confirming correct patient.
  • Assist patients with mobility limitations, including those in wheelchairs, stretchers, or beds, consistently ensuring safety and comfort.
  • Follow established safety procedures when transporting patients via stretcher, wheelchair, or when transferring with lifting devices.
  • Communicate effectively with nursing staff, physicians, and other hospital personnel to coordinate timely, safe patient transport.
  • Maintain cleanliness and proper functioning of transport equipment, including wheelchairs, stretchers, and carts; return oxygen to proper areas
  • Adhere to hospital infection control protocols and safety procedures at all times.
  • Adhere to patient confidentiality policies and regulations at all times.
  • Promptly report patient safety concerns, equipment malfunctions, or incidents to appropriate personnel.
  • Assist in emergency situations as needed, adhering to hospital emergency response procedures.
  • Provide courteous, professional, and compassionate service to patients, visitors, and staff.
  • Perform other duties as assigned, to support hospital operations and patient care.
  • Continuously carry out the Sturdy Health Mission to attain excellence in the provision of healthcare services by consistently fulfilling the commitment to quality and patient centered service.
  • Maintain dignity and rights of patient/family/staff. Listen and respond to inquiries/complaints with respect and sensitivity. Refer complaints to immediate supervisor for investigation and follow-up.
  • Complete 100% of required in-service education. Actively participate in/attend departmental meetings, while engaging in departmental problem solving.
  • Keep informed of changes in policies, procedures, and protocols to ensure compliance.
  • Ensure work area is clean and safe, following departmental procedures.
  • Demonstrates safe use and proper maintenance of equipment, reporting malfunctions appropriately.
  • Comply with established dress code, wearing picture ID badge 100% of the time.
  • Prioritize workload to meet established timeframes. Inform supervisor when timeframes will not be met.

Other Duties:
