title: Mission Analysis Engineer (Entry level) - Millennium Space Systems
description:
Mission Analysis Engineer (Entry level) - Millennium Space Systems

Company:

Millennium Space Systems


Millennium Space Systems, a part of Boeing Defense, Space and Security (BDS), is a fast, agile small satellite company focused on national security space. Our missions have direct impact to global security, like missile warning and Earth observation.

Our team is curious, bold and innovative. We take risks, innovate and explore new techniques and technologies. We influence change because we challenge the status quo. And when we watch our satellites launch, we know each one of us made it happen.

Job Summary:

The Mission Analysis Engineering team is focused on (a) design and development of Concepts of Operations (CONOPS) and Design Reference Missions (DRMs) from key customer requirements; (b) modeling and simulation of satellites, constellations, and system-of-systems; and (c) design and integration of mission data processing algorithms, such as EO/IR image processing or inertial tracking. They are key stakeholders in the design and validation of mission CONOPS and Design Reference Missions (DRM) and are leaders in comprehensive end-to-end software integration, validation, and testing. The team owns the development and validation of the satellite/constellation mission, as well as the predicted technical performance metrics (TPMs) for the program. They are chief architects and implementers of mission data processing algorithms, ensuring mission level objectives are met.

As a member of the Mission Analysis Engineering Team, you will contribute to modeling, simulation, and analysis for a program, study, or proposal. Mission Analysis Engineers don't just execute on ideas - they innovate creative solutions and novel designs to improve our products and solidify Millennium as an industry leader. You will develop methods to simulate mission scenarios and assess end-to-end constellation capabilities; design and deploy image processing, inertial tracking, state estimation, and optimal control algorithms for sensor systems; and provide tools and modeling platforms for validating system performance during on-orbit mission operations. You will work shoulder-to-shoulder with technical and program leadership to ensure that high-quality work products are delivered on time and that the proposed mission solution meets the customer need.

Position Responsibilities:

  • Build and maintain simulations for large satellite constellations to assess effectiveness against mission requirements

  • Own the Electro-Optical/Infrared (EO/IR) image processing algorithms chain, from photon to Warfighter

  • Create models for space vehicle payloads to use in system trades and performance predictions

  • Develop novel algorithms, models, and data processing schemes for MW/MT, RPO, and SDA systems

  • Architect the Concepts of Operation (CONOPS)/Design Reference Mission (DRM) and their associated simulations

  • Collaborate with software and firmware teams to develop platforms for simulation deployment (eg. software/hardware-in-the-loop

This position’s internal job code is Guidance, Nav & Controls Engr. Our team is currently hiring for levels 1/2

This position is expected to be 100% onsite. The selected candidate will be required to work onsite at one of the listed locations.

Basic Requirements: (Required Skills/Experience):

  • Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology (including Manufacturing Technology), Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or non-US equivalent qualifications directly related to the work statement

  • Experience in modeling and simulation of complex aerospace systems using common tools such as Matlab/Simulink, Python, or C++ obtained through coursework, projects, or internships

  • This position requires the ability to obtain a U.S. Security Clearance for which the U.S. Government requires U.S. Citizenship. An interim and/or final U.S. Top Secret Clearance Post-Start is required.

Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience):

  • Experience in aerospace systems design, analysis, and/or operation

  • Experience with EO/IR optical systems analysis and image processing algorithms

  • Experience with government furnished image models like ASSET, PRA Toolkit, or AFSIM

  • Experience in orbital mechanics and kinematic state estimation

  • Experience with satellite space-to-space communication networks

  • Experience with RPO or NMC orbits and associated maneuver planning

  • Technical leadership experience, including requirements V&V, delegation and management of technical tasks, responsible engineering authority (REA) experience, and cost account management (CAM) experience.

  • Possess active TS/SCI clearance

Job Description

Summary
AV is seeking skilled and adaptable FPGA engineers to work as members of a multi-disciplinary team supporting m multiple technology areas. Our Space Tech division develops high-performance electromechanical, electro-optical, control, and communication systems. These solutions include digital signal processing algorithms deployed using System on Chip (SoC) or Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) in combination with General Purpose Processors (GPPs) and microcontrollers.

Position Responsibilities

· Develop and maintain general-purpose and mission specific RTL/Firmware

· Develop and maintain firm ware for peripheral interfaces

· Analog to Digital Converters

· Digital to Analog Converters

· Serial links and communication interfaces (SpaceWire, SPI, CameraLink, 1Gb+ Ethernet, MIL-1553B)

· Develop and maintain automated FPGA firmware platform build scripts

· Deploy firmware to physical devices

· Architect and develop firmware for space electronics, including FPGAs, microcontrollers, and RTOS-based systems.

· Optimize embedded software for radiation-hardened and high-reliability environments.

· Conduct system integration, testing, and validation of firmware in simulated and real-world aerospace conditions.

· Support compliance with space industry standards (NASA, ESA, MIL-STD).

· Other duties as assigned.


Basic Qualifications (Required Skills & Experience)
· Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or computer science.
· 5 years of professional experience designing using hardware description languages (VHDL or Verilog)
· Ability to obtain and maintain a US security clearance.

Other Qualifications & Desired Competencies

· Some experience using Xilinx devices (Zynq, Virtex / Kintex) and toolchains (Vivado / ISE) and/or Microchip devices (RTAX / ProASIC / RTG4) and toolchains (Libero).
· Some experience doing firmware development in embedded systems, preferably for aerospace or space applications.
· Knowledge of (serial) communication protocols and standards.
· Familiarity with multiple clock-domain digital design techniques.
· Familiarity with in-system debuggers and logic analyzers.
· Familiarity with designing and managing FPGA physical constraints.
· Familiarity with Tool Command Language (TCL).
· Proven, demonstrated experience taking VHDL or Verilog designs to a hardware environment.
· Familiarity with the Xilinx SoC devices.
· Familiarity with FPGA floor planning techniques.
· Familiarity with Xilinx System Generator.
· Familiarity with other computing languages (C/C++, Python, Java).
· Familiarity with verification techniques, including linting and constrained random testing.
· Knowledge of RTOS, bare-metal firmware, and hardware-software co-design.
· Experience working with hardware accelerators and space communication protocols.
· Familiarity with other synthesis and simulation environments (Synopsys, Aldec).

Physical Demands

· Ability to work in an office and onsite environment (Frequent)
· Ability to support field testing and integration assignments. (Infrequently)
· Required to sit and stand for long periods; talk, hear, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer and telephone keyboard (Frequent)

No Clearance

title: Expert Architect
description:

The Principal Enterprise Architect, Platform Automation, Operations, AI, and AWS serves as the organization’s highest-level individual-contributor authority and enterprise-wide technical strategist for cloud platforms, platform automation, operational architecture, artificial intelligence, and AWS. The role defines the long-range architectural vision, target-state strategy, governing principles, and enterprise guardrails that direct technology decisions and investments across multiple business and technology functions.

Operating with substantial autonomy and broad enterprise mandate, this position addresses the organization’s most complex, ambiguous, and consequential technology challenges, including matters for which established solutions, precedents, or industry practices may not exist. The role integrates business strategy, operating priorities, technology capabilities, security, resilience, regulatory requirements, financial considerations, and emerging market developments to establish solutions with long-term, enterprise-wide impact.

The Principal Enterprise Architect provides authoritative direction for enterprise architecture decisions spanning AWS cloud services, platform engineering, infrastructure and application modernization, automation, DevSecOps, reliability engineering, observability, AI, GenAI, machine learning, and AIOps. The position establishes the architectural frameworks and decision criteria used by architects, engineers, technology leaders, strategic partners, and delivery teams across the organization.

As a trusted advisor to executive and senior technology leadership, the role shapes enterprise technology strategy, investment priorities, risk posture, and transformation roadmaps. The position challenges existing models, introduces new architectural approaches, and resolves competing priorities across business units and technology domains to deliver scalable, secure, resilient, cost-effective, and strategically differentiated enterprise capabilities.

Success in this role requires exceptional professional mastery, recognized authority across multiple advanced technology disciplines, and a sustained record of defining and leading highly complex enterprise transformations. The role provides technical leadership through influence, establishes expectations for the broader architecture and engineering community, and elevates enterprise capability by mentoring senior architects, distinguished engineers, and technology leaders

Here’s a summary of what Princess is looking for in a Principal Enterprise Architect. Is this you?

Responsibilities:

Enterprise Architecture Strategy and Authority

  • Own and define the enterprise target-state architecture, multi-year technology strategy, and integrated roadmaps across cloud, platform automation, operations, AI, and AWS.

  • Serve as the final enterprise architecture authority for the assigned technology domains, resolving the most complex cross-functional architectural issues and exceptions.

  • Establish enterprise principles, reference architectures, decision frameworks, governance requirements, and non-negotiable architectural guardrails.

  • Translate enterprise business strategy into long-range technology capabilities, sequencing, dependencies, and investment priorities.

  • Anticipate disruptive technology, market, security, regulatory, and operating-model developments and determine their implications for the enterprise.

  • Govern significant architectural decisions whose consequences extend across business units, platforms, products, and multi-year transformation programs.

AWS Cloud Strategy and Enterprise Modernization

  • Define the enterprise AWS strategy and modernization agenda, including target operating models, adoption patterns, platform standards, migration pathways, and optimization priorities.

  • Establish authoritative cloud architecture standards governing scalability, availability, resilience, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, performance, interoperability, financial efficiency, and lifecycle management.

  • Direct the architectural integration of cloud, infrastructure, application, security, data, and operational capabilities across the enterprise.

  • Resolve unprecedented or highly ambiguous cloud architecture challenges with significant implications for enterprise risk, continuity, customer experience, and long-term investment.

  • Evaluate emerging technologies and external market developments and determine where they should materially alter enterprise strategy, architecture, or investment direction.

Platform Automation and Engineering Transformation

  • Define the enterprise platform engineering and automation strategy spanning Infrastructure as Code, DevOps, DevSecOps, CI/CD, orchestration, policy as code, and self-service engineering capabilities.

  • Establish shared platform patterns and enterprise engineering standards that materially improve speed, reliability, security, scalability, and developer productivity.

  • Lead the architectural transformation of fragmented or manually intensive operating models into standardized, automated, policy-driven enterprise capabilities.

  • Set the technical direction for reusable enterprise platforms and services adopted by multiple engineering, infrastructure, application, security, and operational organizations.

  • Establish outcome measures and governance mechanisms to ensure platform investments deliver sustained enterprise value.

Operational Resilience and Reliability

  • Define the enterprise architecture for operational resilience, service reliability, observability, incident management, disaster recovery, business continuity, capacity, and technology risk.

  • Establish enterprise reliability principles, service expectations, and architectural controls for business-critical platforms and services.

  • Determine the architectural response to systemic risk, recurring service degradation, material control gaps, and cross-platform dependencies.

  • Direct strategic remediation approaches for issues that could materially affect business continuity, customer experience, regulatory compliance, financial performance, or enterprise reputation.

  • Ensure operational architecture supports both immediate service obligations and long-term enterprise resilience.

AI, GenAI, and Technology Innovation | 10%

  • Define the enterprise architecture strategy, governance framework, and foundational platforms for AI, GenAI, machine learning, MLOps, and AIOps.

  • Establish enterprise standards for secure, responsible, scalable, and economically sustainable adoption of AI-enabled capabilities.

  • Identify and shape enterprise use cases capable of materially transforming technology operations, engineering productivity, decision-making, and business performance.

  • Resolve novel architectural, security, integration, data, governance, and operational challenges associated with emerging AI technologies.

  • Advise executive leadership on the enterprise implications, opportunities, risks, and investment priorities associated with rapidly evolving technologies.

Executive Advisory and Enterprise Technical Leadership | 5%

  • Serve as a trusted technical advisor to executive and senior leadership on enterprise technology strategy, investment alternatives, architectural risk, and transformation priorities.

  • Present complex technology issues, strategic alternatives, material risks, and recommendations in business and financial terms.

  • Shape and challenge enterprise investment decisions involving cloud, automation, infrastructure, operations, resilience, security, and AI.

  • Lead enterprise architecture councils, strategic design reviews, and cross-functional decision forums for the assigned domains.

  • Mentor senior architects, principal engineers, engineering leaders, and other advanced technical professionals.

Knowledge & Skills:

  • Scope: The position has enterprise-wide and long-term scope, spanning the architecture, modernization, automation, operation, resilience, security, and evolution of technology platforms supporting critical business capabilities. Its authority and influence extend across business units, technology organizations, operating environments, strategic partners, and major transformation programs. The role sets architectural direction across AWS cloud services, infrastructure, applications, platform engineering, DevSecOps, automation, observability, reliability engineering, AI, GenAI, machine learning, and AIOps. Decisions made by this position establish frameworks and constraints for significant technology investments, multi-year roadmaps, operating models, platform adoption, risk management, and engineering practices. The position works across organizational boundaries to reconcile business, technical, financial, security, regulatory, and operational priorities. Its recommendations and decisions may affect employees, customers, partners, technology teams, critical services, and business operations across the enterprise. The role operates with broad latitude and minimal technical oversight. It determines the appropriate architectural methods, decision frameworks, technologies, and interventions required to achieve enterprise outcomes. Matters escalated to this position are typically distinguished by their strategic importance, ambiguity, cross-enterprise reach, material risk, or absence of established precedent.

  • Problem Solving: The position resolves the organization’s most complex and consequential technology architecture challenges, frequently involving conditions for which established methods, precedents, or readily available solutions do not exist. Problems typically span multiple technology domains, business units, operating environments, strategic initiatives, and stakeholder groups and may involve significant operational, financial, cybersecurity, regulatory, resilience, customer, or reputational implications. The role independently structures highly ambiguous issues, identifies underlying enterprise constraints, evaluates interconnected risks and dependencies, and develops original approaches that establish precedent for future decisions. Solutions require exceptional depth and breadth of technical expertise combined with enterprise business judgment, financial awareness, external market insight, and the ability to anticipate long-term consequences. The Principal Enterprise Architect evaluates competing strategic alternatives and makes authoritative recommendations regarding architecture direction, technology adoption, platform consolidation, modernization sequencing, build-versus-buy decisions, operating models, investment priorities, and risk acceptance. The position must balance immediate operational requirements against long-term enterprise scalability, security, resilience, interoperability, cost, and strategic differentiation. The role is expected to challenge established assumptions, identify systemic issues not evident at the project or functional level, and develop new architectural concepts, frameworks, standards, or operating approaches. Decisions and solutions established by this position become reference points for other architects, engineers, leaders, and delivery organizations.

  • Impact: The role has material and enduring impact on enterprise strategy, technology investment, operating resilience, cybersecurity posture, engineering effectiveness, cost structure, innovation capacity, and customer and employee experience. Architectural direction established by this position influences multi-year transformation roadmaps, major technology investments, critical platforms, and the standards by which enterprise solutions are designed, implemented, governed, and operated. The position is accountable for ensuring that enterprise architecture decisions produce measurable improvements in scalability, reliability, security, resilience, speed, productivity, technology economics, and business agility. Errors in judgment or architectural direction could create significant long-term cost, technology risk, operational disruption, regulatory exposure, or constraints on strategic growth. Conversely, successful execution enables the organization to modernize critical technology capabilities, reduce systemic risk and technical complexity, improve operational performance, accelerate delivery, optimize material investments, and responsibly adopt emerging technologies at enterprise scale.

  • Leadership: The Principal Enterprise Architect is an enterprise technical leader and recognized authority whose leadership is exercised primarily through expertise, judgment, credibility, and influence rather than formal reporting relationships. The role establishes architectural direction and professional standards for architects, engineers, technology leaders, delivery teams, and strategic partners across the organization. The position leads cross-functional architecture and transformation efforts involving executive stakeholders, business leaders, infrastructure, cloud engineering, platform engineering, operations, cybersecurity, application development, data and AI, finance, risk, vendors, and other enterprise functions. It resolves competing priorities, creates alignment across senior stakeholders, and secures commitment to enterprise decisions that may require significant change to established technologies, investments, processes, or operating models. The role serves as a trusted advisor to executive leadership and is expected to shape decisions at the highest levels of the organization. It provides independent, authoritative perspectives on technology strategy, architecture risk, investment alternatives, modernization priorities, and emerging technologies, including respectfully challenging proposed direction when it conflicts with long-term enterprise interests.The Principal Enterprise Architect develops organizational capability by mentoring senior and principal-level architects, engineers, and technology leaders; establishing communities of practice; setting standards of technical excellence; and building succession depth across critical architecture disciplines. The role elevates the quality of decision-making across the enterprise by creating reusable frameworks, reference architecture, and governance mechanisms.

For all roles:

  • Knowledge: Understanding of workplace policies and procedures / Familiarity with team collaboration tools and techniques.

  • Skills: Strong time management and organizational skills

  • Abilities: Ability to maintain reliable and consistent attendance / Capacity to be punctual and meet deadlines / Ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues and work as part of a team / Demonstrated professionalism in all interactions and tasks..

Essential/Minimum Qualifications:

Knowledge and technical mastery

  • Recognized enterprise authority with exceptional mastery across multiple advanced technology disciplines, including AWS cloud architecture, platform engineering, automation, operational resilience, and AI-enabled technologies.

  • Expert knowledge of enterprise architecture methods, technology strategy, operating models, architecture governance, portfolio rationalization, and large-scale modernization.

  • Demonstrated ability to integrate cloud, infrastructure, applications, cybersecurity, data, AI, operations, and financial considerations into cohesive enterprise strategies.

  • Expert understanding of systemic technology risk, resilience, cybersecurity, regulatory requirements, architectural economics, and business continuity.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop original frameworks and solutions for complex technology challenges where established precedent is limited or absent.

  • Leadership capabilities

  • Demonstrated success shaping enterprise strategy and materially influencing executive-level technology and investment decisions.

  • Ability to create alignment and commitment among senior stakeholders with competing business, financial, operational, security, and technology priorities.

Essential experience required:

  • Extensive experience operating as a principal or equivalent enterprise-level architect, with demonstrated authority across multiple complex technology domains.

  • Demonstrated success defining and leading multi-year, enterprise-scale cloud, platform, automation, resilience, or AI transformations.

  • Evidence of recognized expertise through industry contribution, professional leadership, patents, publications, speaking engagements, standards participation, or equivalent externally recognized technical accomplishments is highly desirable.

title: Senior Director, Regulatory Transformation & Innovation
description:
Job Description

Senior Director, Regulatory Transformation & Innovation

Job Summary

The Senior Director, Regulatory Transformation & Innovation is a strategic leadership role within Regulatory Operations responsible for driving the implementation of transformation initiatives across Global Regulatory Affairs (GRA). This Senior Director will define and execute a transformation and innovation strategy that modernizes GRA-related processes by enabling new ways of working through application of digitization, AI/ML, analytics, automation, and technology solutions.

Working across GRA and cross-functional partners, the Senior Director will identify, prioritize, and implement opportunities to enhance organizational effectiveness and drive business value, including through innovative approaches to regulatory document development, knowledge management, data utilization, and decision support. The role will ensure innovation efforts are grounded in GRA business needs, aligned to regulatory requirements and enterprise priorities, and focused on measurable business outcomes.

The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in Regulatory Affairs, along with a proven track record of leading transformation, innovation, analytics, AI, or digital enablement initiatives in regulated environments. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, fostering a culture of innovation, continuous learning, and transformation across GRA.

This is a hybrid role requiring a minimum of three days per week onsite at our Boston (Seaport) location.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute a Regulatory Transformation & Innovation strategy aligned with GRA objectives and enterprise priorities, while ensuring delivery of practical business outcomes.
  • Lead strategy, design, digitization, implementation, and continuous improvement of end-to-end global regulatory affairs practices to drive value, including increased efficiencies and reduction of manual work effort (e.g., end-to-end regulatory document authoring, workflow automation, structured content development).
  • Identify, prioritize, and advance emerging opportunities to enhance regulatory capabilities through innovation, AI, analytics, automation, and evolving industry practices (e.g., cloud-based regulatory submissions).
  • Continuously assess external trends, regulatory innovation, and industry best practices to inform strategic priorities and capability investments.
  • Lead innovative approaches to regulatory content development, knowledge management, data utilization, and decision support (e.g., structured content development).
  • Partner with stakeholders to identify and implement advanced technology capabilities, which improve quality, accelerate delivery, and enhance organizational effectiveness.
  • Establish governance, prioritization, and value-realization frameworks to evaluate and advance transformational opportunities across GRA.
  • Collaborate across functions to align transformation initiatives with business priorities, organizational goals, and regulatory requirements.
  • Build strong relationships with external partners, industry groups, and vendors to bring innovative ideas and capabilities into the organization.
  • Serve as a strategic advisor to senior leaders on innovation opportunities, transformation priorities, and organizational readiness.
  • Communicate progress, impact, and lessons learned across the organization to maintain transparency, momentum, and alignment.
  • Define, monitor, and communicate measurable improvements in organizational effectiveness, business performance, quality, agility, and user experience.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of experience in Regulatory Affairs, life sciences, or other regulated industries, with a strong understanding of regulatory processes, regulatory content development, submissions management, or comparable regulated business functions.
  • 10+ years of experience leading transformation, analytics, digital enablement, or strategic technology initiatives that drive measurable business impact.
  • Demonstrated experience leading AI, advanced analytics, knowledge management, or digital transformation initiatives within Regulatory Affairs or other regulated functions.
  • Proven ability to translate innovation strategies into operational execution and measurable outcomes by implementing advanced technologies that enhance business processes and team performance.
  • Demonstrated expertise in change management, organizational transformation, and driving adoption of new capabilities and ways of working.
  • Knowledge of regulatory innovation trends, structured content, data-driven regulatory approaches, and emerging industry practices.
  • Exceptional leadership, communication, collaboration, and stakeholder engagement skills, with proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive alignment across cross-functional organizations.

At Vertex, we embrace continuous learning and encourage employees to stay informed on advances in AI, technology, automation, and industry trends. We seek talent who bring an external perspective, demonstrate curiosity and sound judgment, and thoughtfully adopt new capabilities that improve decision-making, drive innovation, increase efficiency, and help deliver better outcomes for patients.

The Opportunity

Expanding Personal Injury Law Firm seeks a detail-driven professional to support our Strategic Operations Team Lead, paralegals and attorneys by maintaining accurate, well-organized electronic case files throughout the litigation process and ensuring our clients receive timely and precise disbursals at the conclusion of their case.

This role is ideal for someone who is highly organized, team-oriented and an effective communicator - both with internal legal teams and external vendors. Strong communication and computer skills are essential.

The ideal candidate is passionate about professionalism, confidentiality, integrity and is aligned with our firm’s Core Values. We are seeking a cheerful, enthusiastic multi-tasker who thrives in a fast-paced environment and takes pride in helping others.

Objective

Ensure every settled matter is complete, accurate and fully documented prior to disbursement.

Desired Outcomes

  1. Accountable to verify all lien activity, balance verifications, and settlement documentations are finalized and properly saved before the case is prepped for disbursal.

    • Lien Verification Oversight

      • Ensure final lien statements have been received and saved in the file before disbursement.

    • Balance Verification Review

Zoetis Veterinary Medicine Research and Development, Biologics Process Development in Kalamazoo, MI is seeking an analytical scientist at the Sr. Associate Scientist level.

Zoetis Veterinary Medicine Research and Development, Biologics Process Development in Kalamazoo, MI is seeking an immunoassay and / or bioanalytical professional at the Sr. Associate Scientist level. This position will require a highly motivated individual who can effectively collaborate with other team members to advance projects. The successful candidate will be primarily responsible for analytical testing activities supporting vaccine projects from early research through late-stage development and the preparation and testing of biological specimens utilized in the characterization of viral and bacterial antigens. The scientist will help execute testing protocols and will analyze scientific data. The scientist must be able to demonstrate good laboratory safety awareness, rigid aseptic technique, and notebook documentation. Self-motivation, ability to prioritize and work efficiently, have problem-solving skills, and an ability to work independently and within a group are essential.

· Primary techniques for our biologics platform include bacterial and viral titration, ELISA, western blotting, SDS-Page, PCRs, immunofluorescence, Octet, and proof of inactivation assays.

· Prepare reagents, media and buffers as necessary. Order, maintain and stock lab supplies such as common assay reagents, laboratory consumables, gloves, cleaning agents, etc.
· Data entry, verification and handling, record keeping, in accordance with scientific protocol and applicable Standard Operating Procedures
· Perform analytical methods necessary for the characterization of active biological ingredients.
· Run basic analytical instruments such as plate readers, microplate washers and automated workstations.
· Document and communicate results in electronic laboratory notebooks, technical reports, oral / visual presentations.
· Collaborate with other scientists in a variety of technical disciplines including within Analytical Sciences, Process Development, and Biological Research.

· BS/MS in microbiology, immunology, virology, biochemistry, analytical chemistry, veterinary sciences, animal science or other related discipline.
· Minimum of two years of industry experience.
· Academic or industry experience in a laboratory setting, specifically in bacterial or viral characterization.

O que oferecemos?

Estamos em uma jornada revolucionária para simplificar o comércio global, que nos dará a chance de oferecermos um grande impacto na economia mundial, e em sua carreira. Com responsabilidade pessoal significativa, você vai aprimorar o seu conhecimento da indústria e construir comunicação e habilidades comerciais altamente valorizadas em papéis voltados para o cliente – muito possivelmente em um ritmo que vai surpreendê-lo.

Estamos buscando nosso novo Assistente de Logística, que será responsável pela execução dos serviços de transporte de coleta e entrega, controle de insumos da frota, contribuindo para os níveis de excelência operacional e resultado da área.

title: Sr Director, Enterprise Program Management
description:
Job Summary

This role is a unique opportunity to help shape the future of Insulet's next generation diabetes technology portfolio. As the senior leader responsible for driving strategic product development programs from concept through commercial launch, you will play a critical role in accelerating innovation, enabling business growth, and ensuring the successful delivery of technologies that improve the lives of people living with diabetes. Working at the intersection of strategy, innovation, and execution, this position provides significant visibility across the organization and a direct impact on Insulet's long-term product roadmap and market leadership.



Position Overview:

The Senior Director, Next Gen Segment EPMO Leader is responsible for leading teams comprised of various cross-functional team members and external development partners, for the overall development and execution of new programs and technology implementation plans. The role will facilitate the management of the segment product development and sustaining priorities through the clear outlines of scope, objectives and goals, and the successful execution of program activities. This role will also lead various high value strategic programs from project inception to production and commercial launch. This role will provide leadership to Program Managers for the segment scope and work with functional group management to ensure all project elements and milestones are met and continually aligned with corporate strategies and business objectives.

Responsibilities:

  • Segment Team: Participates as a key team member and strategic partner within the segment leadership. Collaborates to align EPMO activities with strategic goals and initiates and leads cross-functional development programs and sustaining activities for all relevant products.
  • Functional Teams: Participates across all functional area VP’s and Management staff in establishing overall product development program goals, scope, resources, and the plans for execution.
  • Governance: Leads the governing and oversight of Insulet product development for the business segment through the Portfolio Decision Team ensuring program status are clearly communicated and issues/risk are escalated and mitigated cross-functionally.
  • EPMO: Provides leadership to the Enterprise Program Management Office to help ensure that Program Managers and cross-functional initiatives and efforts align with overall business strategies in order to achieve successful outcomes per established goals and objectives.
  • Player/Coach: Assists in directing program teams responsible for the development of all approved programs and products with accountability for delivery success as defined through scope, schedule, and resources. Prepared to lead from above or from along-side program teams to ensure timely delivery and execution.
  • Strategic Program Execution: when determined, perform as the overall program leader for large, strategic programs driving plans and execution to ensure products are delivered as defined, on time, and within budgets.
  • People management: Hire, manage, and mentor staff for individual development and leadership in cross-functional product development programs.
  • Specific Focus Area: Provides an unbiased, data-drive perspective of program status and risks to ensure Insulet is objectively managing product development.
  • Performs additional duties as required.

Education and Experience:

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in related field
  • 12+ years of related experience in product development within related field
  • Proven record of product development and implementation in electro-mechanic and/or software products
  • Experience with managing suppliers, external partners, and internal staff (at all levels)
  • Experience in the medical device industry with knowledge related to the FDA design control process


Preferred Requirements:

  • Master’s or PhD degree in related field
  • 15+ years of related experience in product development within related field
  • Ability to influence and manage others both as direct reports, and matrix reports
  • Effective collaborator with strong IQ/EQ
  • Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills
  • Ability to anticipate (“see around corners”) major challenges for hardware and software product development.
  • Ability to organize and judge (triage) priorities.
  • Ability to effectively handle multiple efforts simultaneously

Physical Requirements

  • National and International travel as required (anticipated at ~20%)

Additional Information:



Compensation & Benefits:

For U.S.-based positions only, the annual base salary range for this role is $248,500.00 - $372,700.00

This position may also be eligible for incentive compensation.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:
• Medical, dental, and vision insurance
• 401(k) with company match
• Paid time off (PTO)
• And additional employee wellness programs

Application Details:
This job posting will remain open until the position is filled.
To apply, please visit the Insulet Careers site and submit your application online.

Actual pay depends on skills, experience, and education.

Insulet Corporation (NASDAQ: PODD), headquartered in Massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its Omnipod product platform. The Omnipod Insulin Management System provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. With its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable Pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. Insulet’s flagship innovation, the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the U.S. or by the Omnipod 5 Controller. Insulet also leverages the unique design of its Pod by tailoring its Omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. For more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.

We are looking for highly motivated, performance-driven individuals to be a part of our expanding team. We do this by hiring amazing people guided by shared values who exceed customer expectations. Our continued success depends on it!

title: International Trainee - Asset and Business Developer
description:
Företagsbeskrivning

Vattenfall is one of Europe’s largest producers and retailers of electricity and heat. Our main markets are Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK. The Vattenfall Group has approximately 21 000 employees. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years.

Om rollen

Shape the future of energy.

Are you ready to challenge the status quo, bring fresh perspectives and contribute to solving one of society's most important challenges? We are looking for talented graduates to join the Vattenfall International Trainee Programme. This is your opportunity to accelerate your development, build a strong network across Vattenfall and contribute to the energy transition from day one.

About the traineeship.

This traineeship offers you a unique opportunity to kickstart your career in sustainable business. Each of the trainee positions is distinct, tied to a department within a specific business area and working location. This means that each position has its own tailored responsibilities, challenges and matching profile.

What you will experience

  • Personal and professional growth: Accelerate your development through structured learning, reflection, networking opportunities and real business challenges.
  • Cross-functional network: Connect with trainees and colleagues across Vattenfall's different markets, business areas and locations through programme activities, site visits and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Meaningful contribution: Take on real responsibilities from day one, contribute fresh perspectives and help shape the future of fossil free living.

As Joakim, a former International Trainee based in Stockholm, explains, “I expected beforehand that working at a corporate would mean only serious business. We do focus on learning and growth and bringing new perspectives to the company, but we also have fun and add humor and lightness. I feel like we are the change the company wants to see.”

Your role as a Trainee – Asset and Business Developer

Be part of our initiatives in nuclear, hydro and other asset and business development in fossil free larger scale electricity / energy solutions.

Business Area (BA) Generation is responsible for Vattenfall’s nuclear and hydropower operations. Our mission is to maximize business opportunities while contributing to a reliable, efficient, and environmentally sustainable energy system.

Our staff function Fleet Development within BA Generation, is responsible for strategic planning, optimization of our generation assets, business unit support and follow-up, and business development activities.

This includes conducting analyses, developing strategies, driving strategic processes, and pursuing business and development opportunities. We also monitor the progress of BA Generation’s objectives, track external developments, and perform benchmarking activities.

Your daily activities:

  • Analysing, organizing and planning
  • Making Presentations / Story Lines
  • Supporting managers and colleagues in their daily work
  • Stakeholder management

Kravspecifikation

Who are you?

Whether you want a climate smarter career as an energy specialist, visionary manager, or inspirational project lead in the energy sector, we offer you these possibilities within the Trainee Programme.

As a Trainee - Asset and Business Developer you recognize yourself in the following:

  • Master of Science in Engineering or Business and Economics
  • You have a broad interest in infrastructure asset strategy and business development
  • You are a flexible team player and strong networker who communicates effectively and finds a way forward, even in uncertain situations.
  • You are fluent in Swedish and English, both written and spoken, German is a merit
  • Experience from jobs or assignments within infrastructure, project management or industry is a merit

Whether you aspire to a climate smarter career as an energy specialist, visionary manager, or inspirational project lead, we offer these opportunities within our Trainee Programme.

As Cato, our International Trainee in Amsterdam, mentions, “I feel we are part of leading the change in the energy transition. At Vattenfall we can contribute by adding our individual competencies and core values. I learn how to build relations and be resilient in an international organization.”

To be considered for our traineeship, you should:

  • Be a recent graduate with an academic degree or expected graduation before March 2025.
  • Have maximum one year of work experience.
  • Be fluent in English. Skills in other languages can be a merit.
  • Be willing to relocate for possible assignments throughout the organization.
  • Identify with our principles: active, open, positive and safety.

Location:

You will be working in the department Staff Function Asset Development with Business Area Generation and located in Stockholm (Solna) or Gothenburg, in Sweden.

Ytterligare information

“Vattenfall provides me with the steepest learning curve. We are a group that feels connected by our core values in line with the organization's values: Open, Active, Positive and Safe. We all feel part of a movement that understands the importance of human connection, resilience, and curiosity in energy transition and sustainability.” - Rogier, former International Trainee based in Amsterdam.

The Vattenfall International Trainee Programme is the kickstart of your career within Vattenfall. Over the course of a year, you will combine meaningful work with structured development opportunities, networking, workshops and site visits across Vattenfall's business areas and locations. Each position comes with a competitive salary and excellent remuneration package. Read more about the elements of the Vattenfall International Trainee Programme here.

Application process

We welcome your application in English via the application button on this page. Please include an updated resume. When applying, you will fill out screening questions, including your motivation. No cover letter or motivation letter is needed. The deadline to apply is October 18th, 2026. Selection will start after the application period with online tests, followed by interviews between the end of October to end November.

description:
Our vision for the future is based on the idea that transforming financial lives starts by giving our people the freedom to transform their own. We have a flexible work environment, and fluid career paths. We not only encourage but celebrate internal mobility. We also recognize the importance of purpose, well-being, and work-life balance. The Lead Data Analyst will drive complex analytical initiatives, solve multifaceted analytics problems, and advance analytics capabilities by partnering with business and technology teams. The role will support relationship management and lifetime value analytics while helping the business navigate ongoing CRM and reporting transitions, connect data across systems, and provide reliable visibility into business performance.

This role is an individual contributor position today. It will lead components of cross-functional data projects, provide guidance on analytical methods, tools, and best practices, contribute to functional objectives and roadmaps, and may guide or coordinate the work of others.

What you will do:

  • Lead complex analyses requiring in-depth evaluation of variable business and data factors.
  • Develop dashboards, models, analytical frameworks, and reporting solutions.
  • Help provide clear, reliable visibility into staff and business performance through reporting that brings together data from multiple systems.
  • Investigate business questions by navigating large and complex datasets and identifying meaningful patterns or differences.
  • Connect data across a broad and deep data environment to support reporting and analytical needs.
  • Identify solutions and drive improvements to data workflows and processes.
  • Partner with business leaders to define analytical needs and decision inputs.
  • Provide subject matter guidance on tools, techniques, and best practices.
  • Contribute to functional roadmaps and analytics capability enhancements.
  • Collaborate with technology teams on data structures, pipelines, and automation.
  • Lead cross-functional analytical initiatives and partner closely with stakeholders across different areas and levels of the organization.
  • Apply analytical judgment and intellectual curiosity by questioning inputs, validating results, and considering whether an analysis addresses a meaningful business need.
  • Take increasing ownership of projects and independently drive work as knowledge of the data environment grows.
  • Mentor junior analysts and contribute to best practices and analytics standards as applicable.

What you will bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in analytics, statistics, business, data science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Typically 7 to 10+ years of analytics experience.
  • Ability to comfortably read SQL and use queries to understand expected outputs and data relationships.
  • Experience working with large, highly complex datasets and data structures.

  • Ability to independently lead complex analyses, synthesize insights, and support business decisions.
  • Ability to investigate unclear analytical questions, validate findings, and ask thoughtful follow-up questions.
  • Ability to take ownership of work and manage projects against established timelines.
  • Ability to collaborate across business and technology teams.
  • Finance expertise is not required. The financial concepts used in the role can be learned on the job. Basic statistics may be useful when working with data science outputs, but advanced statistical expertise is not required.

What will set you apart:

  • Master’s degree.
  • Intellectual curiosity and a demonstrated tendency to ask the next question rather than accepting an initial answer without validation.
  • Ability to assess the costs and benefits of an analytical request and appropriately question work that may not have a clear business benefit.
  • Ability to independently connect information across multiple data sources and turn it into a clear analytical story.

description:
At Sunrun, we’re on a mission to change the way the world interacts with energy, and we’re building a company and brand that puts power at the center of life. To do it, we’re designing a dynamic culture where employee development, well-being, and safety come first. It’s why we’ve become the #1 home solar and battery company in America. We’re unlike any other residential energy company. Our vertically integrated model gives us total control over every part of the energy lifecycle – from sale through installation and beyond – so you can find endless opportunities for growth. Come join a career you can grow in and a culture you can run with.

Who We Are

We’re on a mission to make energy more reliable and affordable for more people. We provide an opportunity with storage and solar to help people access greater energy independence without the big upfront costs. Sunrun is the largest dedicated residential solar and storage company in the country and has a mission to bring stably priced resilient power to the masses.


About Sunrun

Since 2007, Sunrun has grown into America's #1 home solar and battery company. We got here by putting our people’s safety and growth first. That’s why we created the Power+ program: to invest in your skills. We train you to work across different teams—from qualifying homes for solar, to installing, to inspecting the final work, and servicing existing systems. This versatility helps limit reduced hours and enhances job security in an industry affected by seasons. It also means you can solve customer problems in one visit, keeping you safely off the road and moving your career forward.

Overview
As a Certified Electrician 2 at Sunrun you will be working on a variety of projects from training and mentoring other Electricians, installing solar systems, performing work for our existing customers, and learning more about energy storage and other new technology.

Physical Demands

title: Internal Communications Lead
description:
TL;DR

This is a strategic operating role at the center of the company, reporting to the Head of Comms with a dotted line to our Cofounder and CEO. Your core job is making sure company leadership communication is clear, consistent, and compounding week after week as we scale. Around that core, you'll own the narrative, the moments, and the rhythms that keep a fast-growing global team aligned, and you'll run the programming lean, with AI doing the production work so your judgment goes where it matters most.

The challenge: when a company doubles in a year across offices and oceans, shared context is the first thing that can break. The warmth of a small team gets diluted by process. Your job is to make sure none of that happens: that every person at Lovable knows where we're going, why, and their part in it, and hears it in a voice that still feels like us.

Why Lovable

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

What you'll do

Be the CEO's communications partner. You'll help make sure what the company hears is consistent from week to week and compounds over quarters. And you'll be a genuine advisor: in the room early, pressure-testing how a decision will land before it's made, and holding a mirror up to leadership when the message and the reality drift apart.

Own the company narrative and operating rhythm. You'll own recurring communications and the strategy behind them: the cadences that ensure every employee understands the strategy, the priorities, and the reasoning, not just the announcements. You'll connect the internal story to the external one so employees hear one narrative, whether it comes from the CEO, their manager, or the press.

Run the moments that matter. Fundraises, strategy rollouts, reorgs and leadership changes, and other high-stakes comms. You'll partner with the Office of the CEO and leadership team to make sure these moments are planned, humane, and land without whiplash: employees hear things that affect them before any rumor mill does.

Make our flagship forums worth showing up for. You'll own the editorial arc of company-wide all-hands, elevate the craft of everyone presenting, and keep these moments warm and personal as we grow past the size where that happens by default.

Build an AI-native internal comms engine. You'll run programming that would traditionally take a team, alone, by defaulting to AI and Lovable itself for input gathering, chasing, aggregating, drafting, and measurement. Human judgment stays where it belongs: editorial calls, sensitive moments, and final approval. If you're still doing production work manually after three months, something has gone wrong.

Raise the bar for how leaders communicate. At Lovable, functions own their own communication; internal comms is not a gatekeeper or a wordsmithing service. Your job is to make every leader and manager a better communicator: standards, tools, coaching, and talking points that equip managers to answer their teams' questions, because managers are the most trusted source most employees have.

Measure understanding, not reach. You'll build lightweight feedback loops that test whether messages actually landed: can people explain the strategy in their own words, do they feel informed, are the whispers going quiet. And when the data says a message isn't landing because the substance is unclear, you'll feed that signal back to leadership rather than polishing the wording.

Who you are

You're an operator and a general problem solver. You build scalable systems from scratch, you're rigorous and structured in how you work, and you have a track record of outstanding achievement in demanding environments. You may have grown up in communications, or you may come from chief of staff, founder's office, strategy, or consulting work with serious writing chops.

You've earned the trust of a founder or CEO. You've been the person a chief executive relies on to sharpen their thinking and their words. You know how to advise without ego, push back with evidence, and keep confidence. Your judgment has been tested on sensitive, high-stakes communications.

You write exceptionally. You know the difference between writing that informs and writing that aligns, and you can do both under deadline.

You're AI-native to your core. You instinctively reach for AI to do the gathering and aggregating, and you're excited to build internal tools on Lovable itself. You see leverage where others see headcount requests.

You read organizations well. You have a feel for the pulse of a company: what people are worried about, where context is missing, which message will land and which will breed cynicism. You listen as much as you broadcast, and you navigate cultural differences across our European and US offices with ease.

You're discreet, low-ego, and steady. You'll sit closer to sensitive information than almost anyone in the company. You handle it with care, you share credit reflexively, and you stay calm when plans change on a Tuesday afternoon.

What you need to know

Strong partnership with our CEO is a big part of the job. Everything else is the platform it stands on. You'll be measured first on whether our CEO's communication is clearer, more consistent, and more trusted because you exist, and second on whether the company stays aligned as it scales.

This function is lean by design. You will not be building a large internal comms team. You'll be building systems, AI workflows, and leader capability that make a large team unnecessary. If your instinct when work piles up is to hire, this role will frustrate you. If your instinct is to automate and equip, you'll thrive.

Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you're deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn't technically "yours" when the moment calls for it.

title: Sr TA Data Analyst
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

The Talent Acquisition (TA) Analytics team’s goal is to transform recruiting from a reactive function into a proactive, predictive powerhouse. A successful candidate is a strategic thinker who is flexible with shifting project priorities and thrives in a fast-paced environment. You demonstrate the confidence to tackle complex, ambiguous problems and the ability to partner effectively with a wide variety of stakeholders.

We seek a highly motivated, energetic self-starter to work directly with TA leadership. Your mission is to ensure they have the data, predictive models, and insights necessary to make informed decisions—often guiding them toward what they need to know, rather than just what they are asking for. You will proactively identify opportunities to enhance data quality, evaluate new recruiting technologies, and unlock insights that shape how we build our teams.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Predictive Analytics & Modeling: Utilize Python or R to build predictive models that forecast pipeline health, candidate conversion, time-to-fill, and long-term candidate quality.
  • AI & Tool Evaluation: Act as the analytical gatekeeper for our recruiting tech stack. Evaluate the ROI, efficacy, and potential bias of new AI tools and automated recruiting workflows.
  • Strategic Metric Definition: Drive the analytics strategy for modern TA disciplines. Define and track complex metrics such as Quality of Hire (QoH), skills-based hiring efficacy, and internal talent mobility.
  • Analytics Engineering & Modeling: Perform robust data modeling, transforming raw system data into structured models for visualization. Consult directly with data warehouse engineers to improve system integrations and data pipelines.
  • Data Visualization Strategy: Lead our visualization and reporting ecosystem. Design intuitive dashboards from scratch and apply advanced design tactics across various BI tools, shifting stakeholders from looking at descriptive data (what happened) to prescriptive insights (what to do next).
  • Ad-Hoc Consulting: Support complex, ad-hoc analytics requests from partners within TA and the broader People Organization.

REQUIREMENTS

  • BS/MS in Engineering, Computer Science, Math, Economics, Statistics, or another highly quantitative discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of work experience in data analysis, data science, analytics engineering, or similar technical roles.
  • Proficiency in data manipulation and statistical modeling using Python or R.
  • Advanced SQL skills and exposure to modern data stores/querying frameworks (MySQL, BigQuery).
  • Proficiency with analytics engineering workflows and version control platforms (Dataform, dbt, GitHub).
  • Strong proficiency with enterprise data visualization tools (e.g. Looker, Power BI, Tableau) and a deep understanding of dashboard design, visualization strategy, and data storytelling tactics.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Cross-Industry Perspective: Proven ability to dive into new data domains and learn them quickly. Note: Prior HR or TA analytics experience is not required; candidates bringing analytical best practices from outside the People space are highly encouraged to apply.
  • Experience auditing AI/machine learning tools for fairness/bias or assessing software vendor ROI.
  • Familiarity with Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
  • Exceptional data storytelling skills: the ability to convey complex technical or statistical concepts to non-technical business leaders clearly and persuasively.
  • Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities with a tenacious commitment to finding the root cause of data discrepancies.
  • Comfortable taking absolute ownership of projects from requirements gathering to final deployment.

For San Francisco, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $131,000 per year - USD $145,000 per year.

Team members gain exposure to complex, high-profile transactions and work directly with senior bankers and clients in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment. The Israel Coverage team is seeking an Investment Banking Associate to join its New York office. The ideal candidate will be an experienced Investment Banking Analyst in line for promotion or an Associate 1/Associate 2 with strong execution experience. The role will focus on advising Israeli corporate clients and supporting cross-border transactions involving U.S. and international investors, strategic acquirers, and financial sponsors.

Key Responsibilities:

title: Leadership Development Programs Lead
description:
We are seeking an experienced Leadership Development Programs Lead to own HR programs and processes for the executive population — the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and their direct reports. Given the confidentiality, governance, and cross-functional coordination these programs require, this role sits at the intersection of talent management, executive development, and board-level reporting, partnering closely with the CEO's office, Chief of Staff, and senior HR leadership.

The ideal candidate brings experience in executive talent management, leadership development, or organizational development, with a demonstrated ability to operate with discretion at the most senior levels of an organization and to translate complex talent decisions into clear, board-ready narratives.

Responsibilities:

Succession Planning & Bench Strength

  • Lead succession planning and bench-strength assessment for the ELT and other critical leadership roles across the organization.

  • Partner with senior executives and HR leadership to identify successor pools, close readiness gaps, and mitigate key-person risk.

  • Maintain and continuously refine succession planning frameworks, talent reviews, and calibration processes for the executive population.

Executive Development

  • Design and oversee executive coaching, assessment, and leadership growth pathways for the ELT and their direct reports.

  • Manage relationships with external executive coaches and assessment providers, ensuring development plans are tailored, confidential, and outcome-driven.

  • Build individualized development plans grounded in 360 feedback, psychometric assessment, and business context.

Executive Onboarding, Offboarding & Transitions

  • Own the end-to-end experience for executive-level talent moves, including onboarding new executives, offboarding departing leaders, and supporting internal executive transitions.

  • Coordinate cross-functionally (HR, Legal, Communications, IT, CEO's office) to ensure seamless, well-governed executive transitions.

  • Develop transition and integration plans that set incoming executives up for early success.

Board-Level Talent & Organization Reporting

  • Prepare board-level talent and organization reporting in close coordination with the CEO's office and Chief of Staff.

  • Translate succession plans, executive development progress, and organizational health data into clear, accurate materials for board and committee review.

  • Maintain the highest standards of confidentiality and data integrity given the sensitivity of executive and board-level talent information.

Governance & Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Serve as a trusted, discreet advisor to the ELT, CEO's office, and Chief of Staff on executive talent matters.

  • Establish and maintain governance processes (timelines, documentation, approval workflows) for executive talent programs.

  • Partner with Legal, Compliance, and Communications as needed on sensitive executive personnel matters.

Requirements:

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in executive talent management, leadership development, or organizational development, with direct exposure to C-suite/ELT-level programs

  • Demonstrated experience managing succession planning and executive development for senior leadership populations

  • Experience supporting executive onboarding/offboarding and leadership transitions in a well-governed, cross-functional manner

  • Experience preparing materials for or presenting to a board of directors or board committee, or working in close partnership with a CEO's office/Chief of Staff function

  • Proven ability to operate with a high degree of confidentiality, discretion, and sound judgment on sensitive personnel matters

Skills & Competencies:

  • Deep knowledge of succession planning methodologies, executive assessment tools, and leadership competency frameworks for senior populations

  • Skilled at executive coaching program design and management of external coaching relationships

  • Experience with 360 assessments and psychometric tools (e.g., Hogan, DiSC, Korn Ferry) at the executive level

  • Strong executive presence and communication skills; able to advise and influence ELT members, the CEO's office, and board stakeholders

  • Excellent project and governance management skills; able to manage sensitive, time-bound processes with multiple senior stakeholders

  • High emotional intelligence and discretion; trusted to handle confidential and sometimes politically sensitive information

Education & Certifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Organizational Psychology, Business, or related field required; Master's degree preferred

  • Certification in coaching (e.g., ICF), leadership assessment tools, or organizational development a plus

title: Sr. Industrial Designer
description:
Our Home & Outdoor division is united by thoughtful design and lasting quality. From kitchens to campsites, we provide consumers with premium, innovative products for life -- in and out of the home. This business unit includes our OXO, Osprey, and Hydro Flask brands, and this role may support one or more of these brands.

Look around your home, and you'll find us everywhere, in your kitchen, living room, bedroom, and bathroom. We are already making your everyday lives better. We are powered by knowledgeable, enthusiastic, and forward-thinking people committed to developing a culture of inclusion. Whether you are just starting your career or in need of a challenge, we recognize, develop, and empower talent!

Position: Sr. Industrial Designer

Department: Industrial Design – Home & Outdoor

Work Location: New York, NY, Hybrid (work 3 days onsite)

Hybrid Schedule: At Helen of Troy, we embrace a flexible hybrid work model designed to support collaboration and productivity. For roles eligible for hybrid work, our standard schedule includes in-office collaboration from Tuesday through Thursday, with the option to work remotely on Mondays and Fridays. Any updates to this model will be communicated in advance. Please note that hybrid eligibility and schedules may vary based on business needs and manager expectations.

What you will be doing:

The Senior Industrial Designer will play a pivotal role in advancing insight-driven design solutions across the Home & Outdoor division for OXO, Hydro Flask, and Osprey.

Building on OXO’s legacy of thoughtful, universal design, this individual will create products that simplify everyday experiences through intuitive, user-centered solutions grounded in deep consumer understanding.

They will help shape Hydro Flask’s next chapter of growth by developing innovative products that blend performance-driven functionality with clean, iconic design, strengthening the brand’s connection to active and outdoor-inspired lifestyles.

In parallel, they will support Osprey’s commitment to purpose-built performance by designing products that embody technical excellence, fit, functional rigor, and user-centered innovation. Working across a diverse portfolio of brands, this designer will translate each brand’s distinct design ethos into compelling, on-brand product solutions.

With the guidance of the Senior Director of Industrial Design, Associate Industrial Design Director and partnerships across various business units including engineering and marketing, this individual will be an advocate for design excellence by leveraging consumer insights and cross functional guidance to make strategic design decisions. This individual will be an active driver of day-to-day responsibilities needed to deliver design solutions at critical gate meetings with key stakeholders.

  • Design and develop new products through strategic thinking and process.

  • Assess user experience associated with ergonomics, user logic and interaction of the product.

  • Ideate product aesthetics associated with form, color and design language.

  • Identify and solve problems with end user needs through rigorous user testing.

  • Apply research and insights to design, ensuring functionality, user experience and aesthetics are on brand to HF & OXO’s identity.

  • Define color solutions in a purposeful and strategic manner which aligns with the business goals.

  • Design within the constraints of manufacturing and cost

  • Align with engineering and Business Units through all stages of design development.

  • Lead design activities through design process gates

  • Implement and organize design activities around schedules and project goals.

  • Manage project timelines, tasks, and functions of projects.

  • Support the optimization of the Industrial Design across HF and OXO by leading the implementation and maintenance of the established Visual Brand Language across the respective brands.

  • Mentor junior designers through guided best practices around user insights and design implementation.

  • Brief junior designers on projects, guiding the execution of direction through various phase gates.

  • Guide development of design and research through frequent, regular reviews, presenting to Design Leadership.

  • Support designers to shepherd designs through the approval process, presenting work to cross-functional teams confidently, clearly, and logically.

  • Monitor and evaluate team to ensure individual and group development.

  • Be the role model for the team creatively and professionally, performing to a consistently high standard.

Skills needed to be successful in this role:

  • Demonstrates strong sense of aesthetics through their work and presentations / portfolio

  • Proven understanding of brand strategy as it relates to Industrial design.

  • Ability to articulate subjective matters in a tactile strategic manner (i.e. color, aesthetics)

  • Experience presenting work and communicating effectively with senior leadership.

  • Ability to work collaboratively and independently.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in industrial design

  • 6 years of experience in industrial design and consumer product development

  • High proficiency in SolidWorks, Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop and Illustrator required), KeyShot, and PowerPoint

  • Demonstrated track record of leading consumer products from concept through commercialization

  • Strong understanding of injection molding and plastics manufacturing processes

  • *Sample Portfolio showcasing work as the primary designer on consumer products is required with the application *

  • Experience with project management tools (e.g., Basecamp, Smartsheet)

  • Ability to travel domestically up to 10% as needed

  • Authorized to work full-time in the United States

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Design Consultancy Experience

  • Experience designing outdoor equipment and gear
