title: Brand Rep-Core
description:
221 - Marketstreet - Lynnfield, MA

Who Are We?

Stand Out For Good, Inc. is a rapidly growing women’s fashion company with 5 unique brands, in 130+ locations, across 38 states. Our stores feel like a sanctuary - a place of beauty from the inside out. From welcoming experiences and warm associates to thoughtfully curated products, our brands are built upon the founding principles of giving back and making a difference in the world.

Our Mission

"Stand Out. For Good". Those four words are more than just our motto, they are why we exist. From Mission Mondays, where 10% of our net proceeds go directly to local charitable organizations, to our long-standing partnership with Coprodeli USA, in which we are in the process of building 22 schools for impoverished communities in Peru, we are committed to giving back in meaningful ways to those in need.

Role Overview

The Brand Representative plays a crucial role in providing a world-class shopping experience for guests while contributing to the overall success and profitability of the retail business.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Welcome every guest with a smile, determine their needs, assist with finding the right merchandise, and offer styling recommendations.

  • Achieve personal sales goals. Identify opportunities to upsell or cross-sell to enhance the guest's shopping experience and increase sales.

  • Work collaboratively with the team to achieve sales goals, maintain store standards, and deliver a world-class guest experience.

  • Maintain product knowledge. Have a thorough understanding of the merchandise offering, including features, benefits, and pricing.

  • Ensure shelves and displays are stocked, organized, and visually appealing.

  • Keep the store clean, neat, and well-maintained to create a beautiful shopping environment.

  • Process transactions accurately and efficiently using a point-of-sale system.

  • Assist with inventory management tasks such as receiving shipments, checking stock levels, and conducting inventory counts.

  • Adhere to company policies, procedures and guidelines, including safety protocols.

  • Process returns and exchanges according to company policy, always ensuring guest satisfaction.

  • Report to work as scheduled, record time worked accurately, and remain flexible to the needs of the business.

  • Must be 18 years or older

​

*Must be available to work nights & weekends*

This position requires extensive periods of standing and walking throughout the entire workday, frequent bending, stooping, reaching, lifting and carrying of items up to 25 lbs., occasional to frequent climbing, sufficient manual dexterity to operate registers, scanners and other electronic equipment, sufficient visual and auditory abilities to complete essential tasks, and sufficient ability to communicate with others to exchange information.

title: Talent COE Intern
description:
Role Overview

The TA Center of Excellence Intern will support the day-to-day operations of Clearwater's Talent Acquisition function, gaining hands-on exposure to recruiting operations, systems, and analytics at a fast-growing, publicly traded SaaS company. This role is well suited to a detail-oriented, process-minded student who wants practical experience in how a modern Talent Acquisition organization runs behind the scenes — not just how individual roles are filled, but how the entire hiring engine is built, measured, and improved.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support day-to-day administration of the applicant tracking system (ATS), including requisition setup, data hygiene, and workflow configuration.
  • Help coordinate interview scheduling logistics across recruiters, hiring managers, and candidates, escalating conflicts or delays as needed.
  • Assist in building and maintaining recruiting dashboards and reports (e.g., time-to-fill, pipeline conversion, source of hire) to support data-driven decision-making.

title: Security Officer I - Part Time - 24 hours per week - Nights - 7PM-7AM - Atlantic Health Chilton Medical Center, NJ
description:
An AH Security Officer 1 is responsible for maintaining a safe and secure environment for patients, staff, and visitors in AH healthcare facilities and corporate locations. This role involves monitoring the premises, preventing unauthorized access, responding to emergencies, and ensuring the enforcement of hospital policies and procedures related to safety and security. Weekend and On- Call / As required

Essential Functions

Security and Surveillance

  • Patrol hospital buildings and grounds to deter and detect criminal activity, suspicious behavior, and unauthorized access.
  • Monitor security cameras, alarms, and other surveillance equipment to ensure the safety of the premises.
  • Secure entrances, exits, and restricted areas to prevent breaches or theft.
  • Control pedestrian and vehicular traffic as needed.
  • Performs all other duties as assigned, including working various 8- or 12-hour shifts (including holidays), being available for call-back assignments, and attending and successfully completing all mandatory training.
  • May be required to lift up to 100 lbs. and stand for extended periods (up to four hours).

Emergency Response to incidents at AH Locations

  • Respond promptly to disturbances (AH Security Assistance) involving Team Members, Patients and/or Visitors. The Security Officer will deescalate the situation and is responsible to ensure the safety of all persons and property.
  • Respond promptly to all acute medical events (AH Medical Assistance) to assist clinical staff as needed.
  • Respond promptly to all fire alarms (AH Facility Alert Fire Emergency) and participate in fire suppression and assist Team Members, Patients and Visitors as needed.
  • Respond and investigate all missing children (AH Missing Person/Child/Infant) and any suspected infant abduction (AH Infant/Child Abduction).
  • Responsible to provide Leadership to our Team Members, Patients and Visitors during any Active Shooter situation (AH Active Shooter).
  • Responsible for assisting all Team Members, Patients and Visitors during any Disaster or Emergency Situation (AH Facility Alerts)

Access Control

  • Verify the identity of visitors and vendors entering AH Medical Centers, Corporate Locations and Off-Site Locations as appropriate.
  • Enforce hospital policies and procedures regarding access to sensitive areas, such as patient rooms, operating rooms, or pharmacies.
  • Issue and manage all Team Member badges.
  • Familiarity with EZ Lobby and Rep Trex computer systems for managing vendor badge access.

Customer Service

  • Provide directions and assistance to patients and visitors.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor while addressing complaints or concerns.
  • Serve as a visible point of contact to reassure staff and visitors that our facilities are a safe environment.

Reporting and Documentation

  • Prepare well written, detailed, and accurate incident reports for all security-related events utilizing the IMC Computer database.
  • Maintain logs of daily activities to include patient scans, helicopter arrivals, property reports, contraband reports, panic button testing, and forensic patients.
  • Establish and maintain effective communication with all Team Members.
  • Proficient in the use of Security Technology to include AHECN distribution, IMC Computer, Mutualink, Victor Video System and ONYX Panel.

Training and Collaboration

  • Work closely with hospital staff, including the nursing and administrative teams, to ensure safety protocols are followed consistent with AH Policies and Procedures.
  • Collaborate with law enforcement and emergency services as required.
  • Participate in the Iron Temple Response Control Techniques (RCT) Training twice per month and maintain a valid RCT Certification with Iron Temple.
  • Complete the FEMA Incident Command System 100, 200 course and the IS 700 National Incident Management System course.
  • Participate in the Emergency Management Decontamination Training.
  • Remain updated on all AH and Protection and Security Services Policies and Procedures.

Education Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Associates degree or bachelor’s degree preferred

Certifications

FEMA ICS 100/200/700 to be obtained within 60 days of hire

Required Licenses

Valid driver’s license with a driving record in compliance with AH’s eligibility requirements.

Experience Requirements

  • Security, law enforcement, and/or military experience is preferred,

Other Desired Skills

  • Security operations and emergency response
  • Investigation and reporting
  • Access control and surveillance systems
  • Strong communication and conflict resolution
  • Physical fitness to handle patrolling and emergency response

title: Creative Production Technologist
description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):

09

The Team:

The 199 is S&P Global's award-winning in-house creative agency that sets the standard for financial industry storytelling through innovative brand experiences. Our tight-knit, globally distributed team values creative excellence, technical innovation, and collaborative problem-solving, working together to transform complex financial insights into compelling visual narratives. You'll join a dynamic environment where creative vision meets cutting-edge technology, supported by colleagues who encourage continuous learning and professional growth.

Responsibilities and Impact:

The Creative Production Technologist offers a unique opportunity to join a small, dynamic team and be the primary technical owner of our new, state-of-the-art studio in Manhattan. This is a blended role for a creative thinker with a strong technical focus. Your primary responsibility will be managing the technical infrastructure of our studio facilities, which includes a green screen/LED wall virtual production stage, a control room, and a self-contained podcast studio.

While technical management is the focus, you are not afraid to pick up a camera, direct a client, or support a podcast recording. You will work closely with a Senior Producer and Associate Producer in New York, as well as our Technical Director in London serving as the main technical expert for the New York facility while also supporting our global teams. You are a self-starter who relishes learning new things and translating creative, story-driven needs into workable technical realities.

  • Serve as the first point of contact for all studio-related technical requests, ensuring equipment readiness for all productions.

  • Look after all studio systems with remote help from our UK based broadcast engineering support team, including the Ross Ultrix Router, Panasonic Kairos vision mixer, and AdderLink KVM network.

  • Log all technical issues, proactively identifying problems to minimize downtime, and act as the main point of contact with our broadcast support vendors.

  • Take ownership of systems administration, ensuring all technical documentation is orderly and up-to-date on Confluence, including technical drawings and asset registers.

  • Administer video-based SaaS systems, including Riverside.fm, CUEZ, Shade.inc, and others.

  • Oversee vendor administration, contractor logistics, and organize site meetings with Facilities Management.

  • Stay updated on industry trends, particularly in virtual production (both green screen and LED wall), and seek opportunities for continuous professional development.

  • You’ll also get to work alongside our local and global production teams to film and edit engaging, customer-focused video and audio projects.

Compensation/Benefits Information: (This section is only applicable to US candidates)

S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $59,212 to $92,566. Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual’s geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses, and certifications.

In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive bonus.

What We're Looking For:

Basic Required Qualifications:

  • 3-5 years of experience in corporate or broadcast video production, with hands on technical and video production experience.

  • Must provide a portfolio of exceptional work that demonstrates your technical and creative production skills.

  • A strong understanding of modern broadcast and virtual production technologies. You are not phased by terms like Dante, BitFocus Companion, 1.5mm pixel pitch, 12G SDI, Ultrix Router, ArtNet, and reference sync.

  • Experience in a corporate video, broadcast television, or live production environment, with proficiency in lighting, audio, camerawork, editing, and graphics.

  • A proven ability to work calmly and effectively under pressure.

  • Experience with both Mac and PC environments and familiarity with the Adobe Creative Suite.

  • You’re security-savvy and have experience looking after systems in a corporate IT environment.

  • Good written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills with a high degree of craft and attention to detail.

  • A keen learner and problem-solver who uses initiative to get the job done.

  • This is an onsite role with the expectation to work in office 5 days per week at our 55 Water Street location.

Additional Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Broadcasting, Media Production, Communications, or equivalent technical experience in corporate video or broadcast video environments.

  • Deep knowledge of control systems, specifically BitFocus Companion for system integration.

  • Familiarity with virtual production on green screen and LED walls; concepts like those used at the Brain Bar are not new to you.

  • Expertise in multi-camera video podcast production and remote shooting setups.

  • Experience with camera tracking systems (e.g., MRMC) and gaming engines for production.

Right to Work Requirements:

This role is limited to persons with indefinite right to work in the United States.

We require all external candidates who reach the final stage of our interview process to attend at least one in-person interview, which is ordinarily at your nearest S&P Global office. This must be completed before we can proceed to an offer.

What’s In It For You?

Our Mission:

Advancing Essential Intelligence.

Our People:

We're more than 35,000 strong worldwide—so we're able to understand nuances while having a broad perspective. Our team is driven by curiosity and a shared belief that Essential Intelligence can help build a more prosperous future for us all.From finding new ways to measure sustainability to analyzing energy transition across the supply chain to building workflow solutions that make it easy to tap into insight and apply it. We are changing the way people see things and empowering them to make an impact on the world we live in. We’re committed to a more equitable future and to helping our customers find new, sustainable ways of doing business. Join us and help create the critical insights that truly make a difference.

Our Values:
Integrity, Discovery, Partnership


Throughout our history, the world's leading organizations have relied on us for the Essential Intelligence they need to make confident decisions about the road ahead. We start with a foundation of integrity in all we do, bring a spirit of discovery to our work, and collaborate in close partnership with each other and our customers to achieve shared goals.

Benefits:

We take care of you, so you can take care of business. We care about our people. That’s why we provide everything you—and your career—need to thrive at S&P Global.

Our benefits include:

  • Health & Wellness: Health care coverage designed for the mind and body.

  • Flexible Downtime: Generous time off helps keep you energized for your time on.

  • Continuous Learning: Access a wealth of resources to grow your career and learn valuable new skills.

  • Invest in Your Future: Secure your financial future through competitive pay, retirement planning, a continuing education program with a company-matched student loan contribution, and financial wellness programs.

  • Family Friendly Perks: It’s not just about you. S&P Global has perks for your partners and little ones, too, with some best-in class benefits for families.

  • Beyond the Basics: From retail discounts to referral incentive awards—small perks can make a big difference.

For more information on benefits by country visit: https://spgbenefits.com/benefit-summaries

Global Hiring and Opportunity at S&P Global:

At S&P Global, we are committed to fostering a connected and engaged workplace where all individuals have access to opportunities based on their skills, experience, and contributions. By valuing different perspectives and promoting a culture of respect and collaboration, we drive innovation and power global markets.

title: International Trainee - Information security coordinator Ringhals AB
description:
Företagsbeskrivning


Vattenfall is one of Europe’s largest producers and retailers of electricity and heat. Our main markets are Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK. The Vattenfall Group has approximately 21 000 employees. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years.



Om rollen


Shape the future of energy.

Are you ready to challenge the status quo, bring fresh perspectives and contribute to solving one of society's most important challenges? We are looking for talented graduates to join the Vattenfall International Trainee Programme. This is your opportunity to accelerate your development, build a strong network across Vattenfall and contribute to the energy transition from day one.

About the traineeship.

This traineeship offers you a unique opportunity to kickstart your career in sustainable business. Each of the trainee positions is distinct, tied to a department within a specific business area and working location. This means that each position has its own tailored responsibilities, challenges and matching profile.

What you will experience

  • Personal and professional growth: Accelerate your development through structured learning, reflection, networking opportunities and real business challenges.
  • Cross-functional network: Connect with trainees and colleagues across Vattenfall's different markets, business areas and locations through programme activities, site visits and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Meaningful contribution: Take on real responsibilities from day one, contribute fresh perspectives and help shape the future of fossil free living.

As Joakim, a former International Trainee based in Stockholm, explains, “I expected beforehand that working at a corporate would mean only serious business. We do focus on learning and growth and bringing new perspectives to the company, but we also have fun and add humor and lightness. I feel like we are the change the company wants to see.”

Your role as a Trainee – Information security coordinator

You will join the Information and security protection teamat Ringhals, where we work to strengthen resilience, protect critical information and support one of Sweden's most important energy facilities. The team supports the organization in information security, personnel security and regulatory compliance, helping ensure that information, systems and processes remain secure and reliable.

As a trainee, you will support and coordinate information security activities across the organization. You will work closely with experienced specialists, the Business Information Security Officer and stakeholders from different parts of the business. Together, you will contribute to areas such as risk management, incident follow-up, governance and compliance. This is an excellent opportunity to build expertise in information security while helping drive initiatives that support the safe and reliable operation of critical infrastructure.

Your responsibilities

  • Support information security activities, including risk assessments, information classification and security-related follow-up.
  • Contribute to incident handling, reporting and continuous improvement of information security processes.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders across the organization to promote awareness and compliance with information security requirements.
  • Assist in interpreting and following up on information security regulations, requirements and governance activities.



Kravspecifikation


Your qualifications as a Trainee – Information security

We believe you have

  • A university degree, or expected graduation before March 2027, in Information Security, Cyber Security, Computer Science, Information Systems, IT, Digital Security or a related field.
  • A strong interest in information security, governance, risk management and regulatory compliance.
  • Fluency in both Swedish and English, spoken and written.

title: Intern - IC Design
description:
At Cadence, we hire and develop leaders and innovators who want to make an impact on the world of technology.

Cadence Design Systems is a pivotal leader in electronic design, building upon more than 30 years of computational software expertise. The company applies its underlying Intelligent System Design strategy to deliver software, hardware and IP that turn design concepts into reality. Cadence customers are the world’s most innovative companies, delivering extraordinary electronic products from chips & boards to systems for the most dynamic market applications including consumer, hyperscale computing, 5G communications, automotive, aerospace industrial and health.

Cadence Ireland is entering an exciting time – we are building a new R&D Centre of Excellence here in Cork. At the IP Group (IPG) we are building world-class high-speed communication and memory IC (Integrated Circuit) products for applications in datacentre SoC processors as well as in consumer, industrial and automotive electronics. Cadence focus on the leading-edge CMOS geometry nodes such as e.g., 5nm TSMC.

Of course, we also have everything else you would expect from a world class technology organization & fortune 100 company, ranked as one of the best places to work worldwide.

We are hiring and looking for interns. If you are passionate about technology and love to learn, work and grow in a multi geography and multi culture organization developing next generation technologies, you should apply as per below:

Job Title: IC Design Intern (IPG Group)

Location: Galway

Reports to: Group Director

Job Overview:

This Internship will introduce you the basics skills of analog and digital IC design for high-speed communication circuits (e.g. 112 Gbps) used in data centre and cloud applications. You will use Cadence tools such as the Spectre spice simulator and the Virtuoso layout tool to design and implement basic IC circuits. You will also participate in team meetings and learn firsthand how an industry design team builds the world’s fastest CMOS communication ICs.

Role responsibilities:

The internship offers the opportunity to contribute to the development of the IC products and get a great insight into the design environment, methodologies and tools of mixed signal IC product design teams.

Job Qualifications:

  • Bachelors or Masters program in EEE
  • Interest in finding out more about analog and digital IC design, signal processing (digital and analog), telecommunications and control theory.

We’re doing work that matters. Help us solve what others can’t.

title: Senior Finance Project Manager
description:
The role

We are looking for a Finance Project Manager to lead and coordinate large, strategically important projects with a significant financial impact on Fastned.

This is a cross-functional role at the heart of the Finance domain. You will work across several finance disciplines and collaborate closely with stakeholders throughout the business. Examples of projects include bank financing, M&A execution, treasury management systems, strategic financing initiatives, and other complex projects requiring strong financial analysis, coordination and execution.

You will bring structure to complex topics, connect the right experts, and ensure that projects progress from analysis and decision-making through to implementation. The role combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution and offers broad exposure to Fastned’s business, financing strategy and growth ambitions.

What you will do

  • Lead and coordinate large finance projects involving multiple disciplines, stakeholders and workstreams.

  • Manage projects from initial scoping and analysis through to execution and completion.

  • Coordinate contributions from teams such as funding and treasury, investor relations, financial planning and analysis, controlling, accounting, tax, and legal where relevant.

  • Prepare high-quality financial analyses, business cases, models and decision materials for senior management and other stakeholders.

  • Assess the financial impact, risks, opportunities and dependencies associated with strategic projects.

  • Translate complex financial and business topics into clear recommendations and actionable plans.

  • Establish project governance, timelines, milestones, decision points and reporting.

  • Identify issues early, manage dependencies and ensure timely escalation when required.

  • Support bank financing projects, including financial analysis, preparation of financing materials, lender coordination, negotiations and execution.

  • Support M&A execution, including financial analysis, due diligence, transaction planning and post-completion activities.

  • Contribute to strategic financing and capital allocation projects.

  • Work with internal and external advisors, lenders, investors and other counterparties when required.

  • Help improve the way Fastned manages cross-functional finance projects and embeds learnings into recurring processes.

What you bring

  • 7+ years of relevant professional experience in finance, investment banking, transaction services, corporate finance, consulting, project management or a comparable field.

  • Experience leading complex, cross-functional projects with multiple stakeholders.

  • Strong financial modelling and analytical skills, with the ability to understand and assess the financial implications of strategic decisions.

  • Experience with bank financing, M&A transactions, due diligence or other high-impact corporate finance initiatives.

  • Excellent project management and organisational skills.

  • The ability to work independently, create structure in ambiguous situations and drive projects forward.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to engage effectively with senior leaders.

  • A pragmatic and hands-on approach, combined with sound judgement and attention to detail.

  • The ability to balance strategic thinking with execution.

  • A relevant university degree in finance, economics, business administration, engineering or a related discipline.

  • Professional fluency in English. Additional European languages are a plus.

Your working style

You are comfortable operating in a fast-growing and changing environment. You naturally bring clarity to complex situations and are able to connect strategic objectives with practical execution. You take ownership, communicate proactively and build trust across teams.

You are not limited by organisational boundaries. Instead, you enjoy working with different finance disciplines and business functions to deliver outcomes that matter. You combine intellectual curiosity with a strong sense of responsibility and are motivated by Fastned’s mission to accelerate the transition to electric mobility.

Join us in building a better future!

We work hard to change the world, but we don't forget to recognise & celebrate our successes, big and small. We put a focus on work-life balance, provide you with genuine work flexibility and have family-friendly policies in place.

Our benefits include:

  • Stock option plan - we believe in shared value creation.

  • Attractive Pension plan fully covered by Fastned.

  • Company bonus plan.

  • 29 holidays. Additionally, we give you 2 ‘Mission Days’ you can use to contribute to Fastned’s mission or to support a cause that is important to you.

  • Fully electric company car.

  • Yearly training budget of € 3000.

  • Access to the mental health platform Nilo Health including 10 sessions with psychologists of your choice.

  • Urban Sports Club Subscription.

  • Additional parental benefits above legal minimum, including coaching via Foundtree.

  • Accessibility to Women's Health platform Flouria.

  • Daily lunches, snacks & drinks are provided at our office locations

  • Company events year-round, including an exciting yearly trip abroad with all employees.

title: Sr Scrum Master
description:
Job Overview:

We are seeking a highly motivated Scrum Master to lead Agile teams in delivering high-quality technology solutions while fostering a culture of continuous improvement. This role is ideal for an experienced Scrum Master who demonstrates strong leadership, program coordination, and stakeholder management skills, with the potential to grow into a Release Train Engineer (RTE) role within a Scaled Agile (SAFe) environment.

The successful candidate will coach teams on Agile principles, drive execution excellence, remove impediments, and collaborate across multiple teams and organizations. Over time, this individual will expand their scope to support program-level planning, dependency management, risk mitigation, and large-scale delivery coordination.

Responsibilities:

  • Facilitate Agile ceremonies, including Sprint Planning, Daily Standups, Sprint Reviews, Release management activities and Retrospectives.
  • Coach teams on Agile values, principles, and best practices.
  • Partner with Product Owners to ensure well-defined and prioritized backlogs.
  • Remove obstacles that impede team progress and delivery.
  • Track and communicate team metrics, delivery performance, and continuous improvement opportunities.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous learning.
  • Support teams in delivering quality solutions while maintaining predictable execution.
  • Collaborate with engineering managers, architects, product managers, and business stakeholders.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.
  • 3+ years of Scrum Master experience in Agile software delivery environments.
  • Strong understanding of Agile principles, Scrum, Kanban, and Lean methodologies.
  • Experience facilitating Agile ceremonies and coaching teams.
  • Strong communication, conflict resolution, and collaboration skills.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders.
  • Experience using Agile management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or Rally.

Preferred

  • SAFe Scrum Master (SSM), Certified Scrum Master (CSM), or equivalent certification.
  • Experience supporting multiple Agile teams.
  • Exposure to SAFe Program Increment (PI) Planning.
  • Experience working in large enterprise environments.
  • Understanding of dependency management and program-level coordination.
  • Demonstrated interest in advancing toward Agile leadership roles such as RTE.

$96,200.00 - $160,300.00

Regional travel up to 35%.

title: Pest Control Technician
description:
Benefits Start Day 1 for Full-Time Colleagues - No Waiting Period!

For more information about our benefits, see below!

We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to many of the world's leading brands and serve consumer and business customers across multiple industries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet."

What do our Pest Control Technicians do?

The primary purpose of this role is to perform our industry leading pest management services for residential customers. You will be responsible for identifying and eliminating pests from residential properties by conducting thorough inspections, determining the type of pest infestation, applying appropriate treatments like pesticides and traps, and providing preventative measures to prevent future infestations, all while adhering to safety regulations and communicating with clients about pest control solutions.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

  • Conduct thorough inspections of client properties to identify signs of pest infestations, damage, and entry points

  • Apply approved pest control products, including chemicals, baits, and traps, to effectively eliminate pests while adhering to safety standards

  • Educate customers on pest prevention methods and the importance of maintaining a pest-free environment. Provide advice on how to reduce the risk of future infestations.

  • Build relationships with customers, schedule and confirm their appointments, help with sales to current customers, and expand our product to new customers

  • Ensure that all pest control equipment is properly maintained, stocked, and in good working condition

  • Adhere to all local, state, and federal regulations regarding pest control products and safety protocols

  • Drive and safely operate a company provided service vehicle (we provide routine maintenance)

Essential Job Functions:

  • Working in tight, confined spaces such as basements, attics, crawl spaces, narrow aisles, or passageways

  • Working around animals, insects and termites

  • You’ll sometimes be working around mechanical parts, vehicles, electrical current, heights and scaffolding, fumes, dust, and chemicals, and we’ll train you how to handle all of these conditions safely

  • Able to work both inside and outside in your local climate in company-provided weather gear

  • Lots of moving around — regularly sitting, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling, up and down stairs, ladders, scaffolding, ramps, and poles

  • You’ll need to wear personal protective equipment (PPE), like an OSHA-compliant respirator

What do you need?

  • Clean shaven face- for safety reasons (rebreathers have to be able to seal your face)

  • High school diploma or GED; related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience

  • Possess a valid driver’s license in state of residence

  • Licenses/certificates as required by federal, state, and/or local regulations (covered by us)

  • Available to work Monday-Friday and weekends as needed

  • Open to learning and becoming knowledgeable in all areas of pest control

  • Solid reading, writing, and verbal communication skills

  • Basic math skills — You’ll need to be able to follow instructions for mixing on product labels

title: Site Coordinator
location: Ontario, OR, Ontario Site, Malheur County
description:
About Oregon Child Development Coalition (OCDC):

Oregon Child Development Coalition (OCDC) is a nonprofit organization serving children and families across Oregon through early education and family support programs. At OCDC, our work has purpose. Every role contributes to creating stronger families, healthier communities, and brighter futures for children across Oregon.

Position Summary:

Coordinates and supervises daily Center activities in compliance with Agency policies and procedures, as well as with Head Start Performance Standards.

Essential Functions:

Ensures effective Center operations by:

• Becoming Acting Substitute Director (as requested) when the Director is out of the building

• Facilitating enrollment information to teachers.

• Arranging childcare for parent meetings when necessary.

• Collaborating with the Education Manager in Child Placement.

• Assisting staff to solve logistics problems (substitutes, purchasing, etc.).

• Coordinating opening/moving/closing of classrooms.

• Guiding the CCD Certification Process.

• Coordinating site-based special events.

• Addressing emergencies and collaborating with Program Director and appropriate Central Office staff for resolutions.

• Coordinating and supervising staffing activities and staffing patterns to include developing staff work schedules, ensuring appropriate staff/child ratios, developing activity schedules for sharing field trips, playground activities, break room, etc.

• Collaborating with Center transportation staff to ensure changes in routes and rosters are appropriately addressed.

• Conducting site inspections as needed and required.

Determines staffing of Centers to meet Head Start and Child Care Division (CCD) regulations by:

• Developing staff schedules to include breaks and lunches.

• Ensuring daily coverage for staff/child ratios including absences, staff and parent meetings, medical appointments, and home visits.

• Providing coverage for classrooms when needed and providing back up for staff when other substitutes are not available.

• Placing volunteers in classrooms.

Participates in the hiring of qualified Center Aids, Floaters and Substitute Teachers by:

• Participating in team interview panels.

• Assisting with the selection of Center Aids, Floaters and Substitute Teachers.

• Participating in orientation of new staff to the Center.

• Ensuring that Center Aids, Floaters and Substitute Teachers receive ongoing training and technical assistance.

•Facilitates child abuse reporting and follow-up process in collaboration with Management staff.

Provides information and services to parents and Center by:

• Giving tours to visitors and parents.

Ensures and coordinates program integration in the Center by:

• Meeting regularly and working cooperatively with Program Director, Component Coordinators, Family Service Workers (FSW), on-site staff, Cooks, Custodians, and Transportation staff.

• Being a participant on the County Management Team.

• Maintaining Center information and communication binders/bulletin boards.

• Providing positive, constructive input in meetings, reports, budgets, and planning.

• Completing monthly reports on time.

• Establishing open, positive communication and interaction with all staff.

• Participating in Center planning and program reviews.

• Fostering an understanding of Head Start, its mission, goals, objectives, and program services.

Maintains appropriate education equipment and supply inventory by:

• Distributing classroom supplies on an ongoing basis.

• Completing a thorough supply inventory annually.

• Checking stock to determine inventory level, coordinating orders for supplies and verifying receipt in accordance with OCDC purchasing guidelines.

• Doing all warehouse ordering and receiving for classroom supplies (including diapers, gloves, toys, etc).

Maintains Center staff performance results by:

• Supervising Center Aides, Floaters, Substitute Teachers, and volunteers with input from the Education Team.

• Providing guidance and positive reinforcement to include conducting and reviewing staff performance and holding monthly meetings.

• Developing a process to ensure program effectiveness through employee performance plans.

• Planning, monitoring, and appraising job results to include review of documentation, memos, notes, and other data.

• Implementing staff disciplinary procedures in accordance with OCDC policy and procedures.

• Documenting site staff concerns and investigations.

• Reviewing and authorizing staff time records and overtime to ensure compliance with OCDC policies and procedures in regard to wage and hour laws and regulations.

• Ensuring compliance with OCDC occupational safety and health standards.

•Consults with Program Director/Program Manager on a daily basis to review program issues and activities, defines and resolves problems, and provides update on any Center changes or activities.

•Maintains a positive image in the community and advocates for children, low-income families and any other groups that require OCDC services.

Maintains confidence and protects OCDC operations by:

• Keeping information confidential.

Provides emergency services as a Mandatory First Responder by:

• Responding to child/adult emergencies using First Aid and CPR skills.

• Contacting appropriate medical personnel.

• Ensuring documentation related to incident is completed.

• Participating in fire drills and assisting in the safe evacuation of children.

Continually applies safety practices in all facets of the performance of duties by:

• Complying with OCDC safety standards.

• Supporting participation of a safe environment by conducting safety checks.

• Immediately reporting any unsafe or hazardous working conditions and/or any injury.

• Coordinating and developing the Center safety committee.

• Conducting facility inspections.

• Enforcing adherence to regulations.

• Ensuring a safe and healthy environment for children and staff.

• Collaborating with Management staff for the prompt completion of injury investigations, corrective actions, and inspections as required.

Other responsibilities:

• Conducts weekly PIPs

• Performing other work related or assigned duties.

Education and Experience Requirements:

  • AA/AS degree in Early Childhood Education or closely related field

  • OR

  • High School Diploma/GED with 1 year classroom experience in an education environment utilizing supervisory skills.

title: Expert Architect
description:
One of the best-known names in cruising, Princess is the world’s leading international premium cruise line and tour company, carrying millions of guests each year to hundreds of destinations around the globe. We give our guests the Medallion Class experience others simply can’t. The Love Boat promises something for everyone.

The Principal Enterprise Architect, Advanced Performance Monitoring and Middleware serves as the organization’s highest-level professional authority and global thought leader for application performance monitoring, enterprise observability, middleware, integration platforms, and operational telemetry. The role defines and materially shapes the long-term global technology strategy, enterprise architecture, governance model, and innovation agenda for these disciplines across a complex, multinational operating environment.

This position applies broad and comprehensive expertise in leading-edge theories, technologies, and architectural practices to identify and solve the organization’s most complex and consequential technology challenges. The role establishes mandatory enterprise standards and target-state architectures that govern the design, reliability, scalability, security, resilience, and performance of mission-critical services supporting guest-facing, shipboard, shoreside, and corporate operations.

The Principal Enterprise Architect leads the organization’s largest and most strategically significant multidisciplinary architecture and transformation initiatives, with impact across brands, business units, geographies, technology platforms, and external strategic partners. The role proactively identifies emerging technologies and creates innovative architecture models, engineering practices, and industry-leading solutions that influence the future direction of the organization and advance the broader observability and middleware profession.

Operating with substantial autonomy, the role advises senior executives on technology strategy, enterprise risk, platform investments, and long-term capability development. The position represents the organization externally with technology providers, professional communities, industry forums, and strategic partners and is recognized as a leading authority in the field.

Here’s a summary of what Princess is looking for in a Principal Enterprise Architect. Is this you?

Responsibilities:

Global Enterprise Architecture and Strategy

  • Define, own, and materially shape the long-term global strategy, target-state architecture, and innovation roadmap for enterprise observability, application performance monitoring, middleware, integration, and telemetry capabilities.

  • Serve as the organization’s highest technical authority for these disciplines, establishing mandatory architecture principles, enterprise standards, reference architectures, governance requirements, and investment priorities.

  • Translate enterprise business strategy, operational priorities, and emerging industry developments into multiyear technology strategies that shape the future direction of mission-critical platforms and services.

  • Determine the objectives and architectural direction for the organization’s most complex technology assignments and independently design innovative solutions where established methods or industry precedent do not exist.

  • Advise senior executives on significant technology investments, strategic risks, emerging capabilities, and decisions affecting the long-term reliability, resilience, scalability, and competitiveness of the business.

  • Represent the organization as an external thought leader through strategic technology partnerships, professional forums, industry working groups, and relationships with leading technology providers.

  • Create and promote innovative architecture practices and technology capabilities that establish new standards for the organization and contribute to the advancement of the observability, middleware, and enterprise architecture professions.

Advanced Performance Monitoring and Observability

  • Set the global architectural direction for enterprise APM, digital experience monitoring, infrastructure monitoring, network observability, log management, distributed tracing, analytics, and operational intelligence.

  • Lead the design and evolution of a unified, enterprise-wide observability ecosystem spanning hybrid cloud, multicloud, on-premises, shipboard, shoreside, containerized, and distributed application environments.

  • Establish enterprise policies and standards for telemetry architecture, service-level indicators, service-level objectives, performance engineering, data retention, event correlation, predictive analytics, and automated remediation.

  • Direct the architectural response to the organization’s most complex and consequential reliability and performance challenges, including issues that cross multiple technology disciplines, business units, platforms, and geographic environments.

  • Pioneer the application of artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation, and predictive analytics to identify emerging risks, prevent service disruption, accelerate root cause identification, and improve global operational resilience.

  • Ensure observability capabilities are embedded as foundational architectural requirements within cloud engineering, platform engineering, Infrastructure-as-Code, DevSecOps, and CI/CD practices.

Middleware, Integration, and Event-Driven Architecture

  • Define the global target-state architecture and strategic roadmap for middleware, messaging, event streaming, API management, enterprise integration, and service-mesh technologies supporting the organization’s most critical business services.

  • Establish mandatory enterprise architecture patterns for highly available, scalable, secure, and resilient integration services across business-critical and customer-facing environments.

  • Lead major modernization initiatives that transform legacy middleware and integration environments into cloud-native, API-led, and event-driven technology ecosystems.

  • Determine the architectural approach for complex cross-platform integration challenges where solutions require the creation of new methods, models, or technical standards.

  • Govern platform lifecycle, technology selection, vendor strategy, architectural exceptions, and long-range investment decisions for enterprise middleware and integration capabilities.

  • Influence strategic product roadmaps with technology vendors and partners to ensure future capabilities address the organization’s global operational and architectural requirements.

Enterprise Innovation and Industry Thought Leadership

  • Establish and lead the global innovation agenda for observability, performance engineering, middleware, integration, and operational intelligence.

  • Identify emerging technologies, theories, and engineering practices with the potential to fundamentally improve business resilience, guest experience, operational performance, and technology economics.

  • Develop original architecture models, frameworks, and engineering approaches that address challenges for which external leading practices or established precedents are insufficient.

  • Serve as a recognized external thought leader and organizational spokesperson in the discipline, sharing architecture perspectives and innovative practices with industry forums, professional bodies, technology partners, and peer organizations.

  • Build strategic relationships with leading technology companies, research organizations, and professional networks to influence product direction, promote innovation, and advance industry practices.

  • Maintain the organization’s position at the forefront of global observability, middleware, and enterprise architecture capabilities.

Leadership of Global Multidisciplinary Initiatives

  • Lead the organization’s largest and most strategically significant multidisciplinary architecture programs and initiatives, with material impact across brands, business units, countries, technology domains, and operational environments.

  • Provide authoritative technical direction to senior architects, engineering leaders, cybersecurity specialists, application teams, cloud teams, infrastructure teams, vendors, and external strategic partners.

  • Mobilize and align multidisciplinary stakeholders around complex architecture decisions where priorities, technical perspectives, business requirements, and risk tolerances may conflict.

  • Exercise enterprise-level decision authority through architecture governance forums, including approval or rejection of material architecture designs, technology selections, standards exceptions, and platform strategies.

  • Establish formal professional networks and communities of practice that advance technical capability, architecture maturity, innovation, and succession depth across the organization.

  • Mentor senior technical leaders and recognized experts while defining expectations for professional excellence within the discipline.

Business Impact, Risk, and Investment

  • Shape multiyear technology investment strategies and portfolio priorities for enterprise observability, middleware, integration, telemetry, and associated platform capabilities.

  • Evaluate and communicate the global business implications of complex architecture decisions, including impacts on guest experience, business continuity, operational resilience, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, technology cost, and strategic agility.

  • Proactively identify systemic risks and future technology constraints that could materially affect the management, direction, or long-term performance of the business.

  • Provide independent recommendations to senior executives regarding major investments, technology adoption, enterprise risk acceptance, vendor strategy, and platform modernization.

  • Define measurable enterprise outcomes for reliability, resilience, performance, automation, and operational maturity and hold multidisciplinary initiatives accountable for achieving those outcomes.

  • Negotiate critical technical and commercial matters with strategic technology providers and materially influence enterprise policies, technology standards, and investment decisions.

Knowledge & Skills:

  • Scope: The Principal Enterprise Architect, Advanced Performance Monitoring and Middleware is the highest-level professional individual contributor and recognized technical authority for observability, application performance monitoring, middleware, integration platforms, event-driven architecture, and operational telemetry. The role has global scope across a complex, multinational technology environment and establishes the strategy, standards, target-state architectures, governance requirements, and innovation priorities that guide these capabilities across brands, business units, countries, shipboard operations, shoreside operations, cloud platforms, on-premises environments, and external technology ecosystems. Decisions made by this role shape multiyear technology investments, enterprise platform strategies, architecture policies, and the reliability and resilience of mission-critical business services. The role leads the largest multidisciplinary initiatives within its area of specialization and exercises enterprise influence through technical authority, architecture governance, executive advisory responsibilities, external thought leadership, and strategic relationships with technology providers and industry organizations.

  • Problem Solving: The role independently identifies and resolves the organization’s most complex, ambiguous, and unprecedented architecture and technology challenges, including matters with significant implications for business direction, global operations, guest experience, enterprise risk, and long-term technology investment. Solutions frequently cannot be derived from established practices or existing precedent. The role is expected to apply first-principles thinking, broad multidisciplinary expertise, advanced analytical judgment, and original innovation to create new architecture models, engineering methods, and enterprise standards. The Principal Enterprise Architect anticipates systemic risks and future technology constraints before they become operational issues; reconciles conflicting requirements across technology, security, business, regulatory, and operational stakeholders; and determines strategic solutions where available information is incomplete, and the consequences of decisions extend across multiple brands, platforms, geographies, and business functions.

  • Impact: The role has significant, long-term impact on the strategic direction, operational resilience, technology economics, and digital capabilities of a complex global business. Architecture decisions and standards established by this position influence the performance, availability, scalability, security, and continuity of mission-critical services supporting guest-facing, shipboard, shoreside, and corporate operations. The role materially influences multiyear investment decisions, global modernization programs, technology-provider strategies, enterprise risk posture, and the adoption of emerging capabilities. Its innovations create new organizational capabilities and are expected to influence leading practices beyond immediate organization. The position’s recommendations are relied upon by senior executives and technology leaders when making decisions with broad financial, operational, strategic, and reputational implications.

  • Leadership: The Principal Enterprise Architect leads through recognized expertise, strategic vision, architecture authority, and organizational influence. Although the position has no direct reports, it provides authoritative direction to senior architects, engineers, technology leaders, vendors, and multidisciplinary teams working across organizational and geographic boundaries. The role leads the organization’s largest and most strategically significant initiatives within its disciplines, creates alignment among senior stakeholders with competing priorities, and negotiates critical architecture, investment, risk, and policy matters. It chairs or provides final technical authority within relevant architecture governance forums and establishes the standards by which enterprise solutions are evaluated. The role also serves as a key external spokesperson for the organization, builds formal professional networks, influences strategic technology partners, and advances the organization’s reputation and capabilities within the broader technology profession.

For all roles:

  • Knowledge: Understanding of workplace policies and procedures / Familiarity with team collaboration tools and techniques.

  • Skills: Strong time management and organizational skills

  • Abilities: Ability to maintain reliable and consistent attendance / Capacity to be punctual and meet deadlines / Ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues and work as part of a team / Demonstrated professionalism in all interactions and tasks.

  • Problem solving: Handles complex, high-stakes guest issues requiring rapid, independent decision-making and creative solutions. Balances company interests with guest satisfaction, often under time-sensitive and high-pressure conditions.

  • Impact: Directly influences guest satisfaction metrics (NPS), financial outcomes, and company reputation. Sets precedents for future guest relations and compensation practices

  • Leadership: Provides leadership and guidance to both shipboard and shoreside teams during incidents. Manages cross-departmental collaboration and ensures consistent implementation of senior leadership directives

Essential/Minimum Qualifications:

Essential qualifications and experience

  • Demonstrated success defining enterprise technology strategy and leading large, multidisciplinary transformations with impact across business units, geographic regions, and technology domains.

  • Demonstrated record of creating innovative architecture solutions, frameworks, or engineering practices for complex problems where established precedent was unavailable or insufficient.

  • Recognized thought leadership within the observability, middleware, integration, performance engineering, or enterprise architecture profession.

  • Experience advising senior executives and influencing material technology investments, enterprise policies, platform strategies, and risk decisions.

  • Experience representing an organization with strategic vendors, professional bodies, industry forums, or external technology communities.

Preferred qualifications

  • Relevant advanced certifications in enterprise architecture, cloud architecture, Kubernetes, observability, middleware, or performance engineering.

  • Published thought leadership, professional presentations, standards contributions, patents, recognized innovations, or leadership in relevant industry communities.

Essential experience required:

  • 15+ years of experience in enterprise architecture or senior technical leadership roles.

  • Deep expertise in Application Performance Monitoring (APM) and observability platforms.

  • Extensive experience designing and supporting enterprise middleware environments.

  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, networking, cloud architecture, and system performance optimization.

  • Experience with enterprise-scale monitoring, logging, alerting, and telemetry platforms.

  • Proven ability to lead large-scale technology transformation initiatives.

Preferred qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related discipline.

title: International Trainee - Associate Project Manager
description:
Company Description

Vattenfall is one of Europe’s largest producers and retailers of electricity and heat. Our main markets are Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK. The Vattenfall Group has approximately 21 000 employees. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years.



Job Description


Shape the future of energy.

Are you ready to challenge the status quo, bring fresh perspectives and contribute to solving one of society's most important challenges? We are looking for talented graduates to join the Vattenfall International Trainee Programme. This is your opportunity to accelerate your development, build a strong network across Vattenfall and contribute to the energy transition from day one.

About the traineeship.

This traineeship offers you a unique opportunity to kickstart your career in sustainable business. Each of the trainee positions is distinct, tied to a department within a specific business area and working location. This means that each position has its own tailored responsibilities, challenges and matching profile.

What you will experience

  • Personal and professional growth: Accelerate your development through structured learning, reflection, networking opportunities and real business challenges.
  • Cross-functional network: Connect with trainees and colleagues across Vattenfall's different markets, business areas and locations through programme activities, site visits and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Meaningful contribution: Take on real responsibilities from day one, contribute fresh perspectives and help shape the future of fossil free living.

As Joakim, a former International Trainee based in Stockholm, explains, “I expected beforehand that working at a corporate would mean only serious business. We do focus on learning and growth and bringing new perspectives to the company, but we also have fun and add humor and lightness. I feel like we are the change the company wants to see.”

Your role as a Trainee – Associate Project Manager

You will join Project Central, Vattenfall Power Solutions’ central function for project governance, project values and project quality. We work across the organization to improve project delivery and support our Business Unit’s leadership in prioritizing, governing and following up on strategic development initiatives and investments.

As a trainee, you will contribute to the development of our PMO capabilities, helping to improve processes, reporting, portfolio insights and performance measurement. You will work closely with project managers, PMO specialists, business stakeholders and management teams across the business unit.

During your first year, you will gain hands-on experience in project governance, portfolio management, business improvement and data-driven decision making. Your work will help strengthen Vattenfall’s ability to deliver important investments safely, efficiently and with maximum business value.

Your responsibilities:

  • Support the development of PMO processes, methods and governance
  • Contribute to reporting, KPI development and project analytics to management team
  • Identify improvement opportunities and support implementation initiatives
  • Assist in developing management dashboards and decision support material
  • Collaborate with stakeholders across business areas and project organizations

Qualifications

Your qualifications as a Trainee - Associate Project Manager

  • University degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering and Management, Business Administration or a related field
  • Strong interest in project management, business improvement and organizational development
  • Good analytical skills and ability to work with data and reporting
  • Fluent in both Swedish and English, both spoken and written

You should also recognize yourself in

  • Curious, proactive and eager to learn
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills
  • Structured and comfortable working with several stakeholders
  • Enjoys identifying improvements and turning ideas into action

Whether you aspire to become an energy specialist, project manager, digital expert, engineer or future leader, the International Trainee Programme offers opportunities to explore your potential and build a meaningful career.

As Cato, a former International Trainee based in Amsterdam, mentions, “I feel we are part of leading the change in the energy transition. At Vattenfall we can contribute by adding our individual competencies and core values. I learn how to build relations and be resilient in an international organization.”

To be considered for our traineeship, you should:

  • Have completed, or expect to complete, an academic degree before the programme starts in March 2027.
  • Have no more than one year of relevant work experience after graduation, excluding internships and working-student roles.
  • Be fluent in English.
  • Be available for the full-time programme from its start date.
  • Have the right to work in the country where the position is based, or meet the stated work-permit requirements.
  • Be open to mobility opportunities and collaborating across different locations.
  • Demonstrate curiosity, initiative and growth mindset while sharing our values: Active, Open, Positive and Safe.

Location:

You will be working in the department Project Central at BU Vattenfall Power Solutions and located in Solna or Gothenburg, Sweden.

Additional Information

Our offer

“Vattenfall provides me with the steepest learning curve. We are a group that feels connected by our core values in line with the organization's values: Open, Active, Positive and Safe. We all feel part of a movement that understands the importance of human connection, resilience, and curiosity in energy transition and sustainability.”

- Rogier, former International Trainee based in Amsterdam.

The Vattenfall International Trainee Programme is the kickstart of your career within Vattenfall. Over the course of a year, you will combine meaningful work with structured development opportunities, networking, workshops and site visits across Vattenfall's business areas and locations. Each position comes with a competitive salary and excellent remuneration package. Read more about the elements of the Vattenfall International Trainee Programme here.

Application process

We welcome your application in English via the application button on this page. Please include an updated resume. When applying, you will fill out screening questions, including your motivation

title: Corporate Communications & Public Affairs
description:
TL;DR

You're a communications professional who can plan and execute the work that advances Lovable's objectives across EU and Swedish policy environments, making sure our voice is heard on the issues that matter most. You'll pair sharp corporate communications with real policy fluency — working closely with internal teams and external partners to help policymakers, media, and other stakeholders understand Lovable's perspective on the key files and issues that shape the environment we operate in.

This is a balanced role, equal parts policy operator and corporate communicator. You'll report to the European Communications and Public Affairs Lead.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What you'll do

This role makes sure Lovable has a credible, constructive voice in the rooms that matter — building a presence worth listening to and developing clear positions that reflect what Lovable actually builds and believes.

Advocate Lovable's positions on key policy files. You'll build and run our engagement with policy representatives across EU and Swedish institutions.

Own corporate communications on policy issues. Statements, briefings, op-eds, speaking moments, and the proactive announcements that build credibility over time. You'll develop the strategy, write the materials, manage media relationships, and make sure each piece reinforces the others.

Track the regulatory agenda and turn it into a point of view. You'll monitor the files that affect us and develop clear positions that reflect the company's reality and ambitions.

Build coalitions and work through industry. You'll represent Lovable in trade associations and industry groups, finding shared causes that move issues forward.

Act as a comms and policy partner to our cross-functional team. You'll work closely with the communications and cross-functional teams in preparing for engagements with policymakers, institutions, and press, strengthening the company’s voice in the European AI debate.

Who you are

You've operated in and around the policy world. That might mean an EU institution, a trade association, a think tank, or a public affairs firm. Wherever you've been, you know how a file moves from idea to law, and you can read the politics, formal and informal, that determine what actually happens.

You understand policy and can communicate it. You have experience from both policy work and corporate communications, and you're equally comfortable speaking to policymakers and media alike.

You can drive an issue forward in a complex political environment. You're comfortable with ambiguity and competing agendas, and you know how to prioritize when everything feels urgent.

You're a sharp writer with editorial judgment. You can turn a dense regulatory development into a crisp briefing, opinion piece or clean position statement.

You connect dots that other people don't see. You look at a piece of draft legislation and think ahead on what it means for the industry as well as what Lovable should say and to whom.

You're a genuine cross-functional collaborator. You work easily with cross-functional stakeholders, external partners, and coalitions. You don't wait to be invited into the room. You're not precious about who gets credit. You just make things work.

You're deeply curious about AI, technology policy, and the industry landscape. You keep up with what happens in the world instinctively — the news, the regulatory moves, the debates as they unfold. You understand where the conversation is heading well enough to spot a risk or an opportunity before someone hands it to you.

What you need to know

This is not a role where you set the strategy and hand off execution. You'll be writing the first drafts of our position statements, building the relationships and showing up in the room as a Lovable representative.

We move fast and plans change. The job runs on two clocks at once: you'll react to the urgent issue that lands today while building the relationships and positions that set us up for success in the long term. If you need a settled environment with predictable workflows, this will be frustrating. If you find that kind of pace energizing, you'll love it.

We're building public affairs and communications at a company that is itself being built. That means you'll have real influence over how this function develops in Europe: the positions, the relationships, the standards. That's the upside of being early.

Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you're deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn't technically "yours" when the moment calls for it.

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

title: Senior Specialist Regulatory Operations  (Electronic Submissions)
description:
Mylan, Lda.

Viatris is a global healthcare company uniquely positioned to bridge the traditional divide between generics and brands, combining the best of both to more holistically address healthcare needs globally. With a mission to empower people worldwide to live healthier at every stage of life, we provide access at scale, currently supplying high-quality medicines to approximately 1 billion patients around the world annually and touching all of life's moments, from birth to the end of life, acute conditions to chronic diseases.

For those driven to live their lives with purpose, Viatris helps employees realise their full potential by creating a collaborative culture that fosters courage and resilience. Viatris is more than just a place to work. This is a place to make a difference in the world.

The Role & What You Will Be Doing

With minimal supervision, support the end-to-end publishing and submission of regulatory dossiers for new and existing products in electronic format to meet company standards, agency requirements and defined timelines. This includes quality control, validation, electronic transmission, and archiving of submissions. Utilise specialised publishing, document management and RIM tools as appropriate. Troubleshoot technical issues, manage submission schedules, and serve as a subject matter expert for publishing activities. Contribute to process improvements, system support, and regulatory project work, while also mentoring junior colleagues and providing leadership support as needed.

Every day, we rise to the challenge to make a difference and here’s how the Senior Specialist, Electronic Submissions role will make an impact:

  • Publish, transmit, and archive Marketing (MA) Applications and maintenance submissions in eCTD or non-eCTD formats as appropriate, for new and existing products, in a timely manner to meet deadlines and Service Level Agreements.
  • Perform QC and technical validation of electronic submissions to ensure compliance with internal standards and external criteria before delivery to the Regulatory Users for internal review/approval.
  • Manage and monitor publishing schedules, coordinate global support during resource constraints, and provide workload and project summaries at team meetings or to leadership
  • Serve as the primary contact and Subject Matter Expert (SME) for publishing queries across Regulatory Affairs and cross-functional disciplines.
  • Contribute to the creation, maintenance, and training of internal regulatory system guidelines within scope of this role.
  • Develop and maintain an advanced working knowledge of publishing software and other regulatory systems within scope of this role
  • Mentor junior colleagues in publishing practices, workload management and software system use
  • Act as a backup for management in their absence, including coordination of workload for the team, meeting attendance and answering queries

  • Bachelor’s degree with focus on Information Management, Bio Science, Business Administration or equivalent preferred. However, a combination of experience and/or education will be taken into consideration.
  • Profound knowledge in the regulatory operations sector, especially in publishing and dossier submission management or related areas.
  • Must maintain expert knowledge of eCTD requirements for multiple Health Authorities
  • Expertise with MS Office, Adobe Acrobat Professional, Document Management Systems (DMS), eCTD Publishing software and registrations management systems and associated global publishing processes and related regulations.
  • Due to the international nature of this position, you have a very good command of written and spoken English.
  • Must possess ability to multi-task and manage multiple projects and deadlines. Ability to work in a fast paced environment. Must possess excellent attention to detail and propensity to learn.
  • Personally, you are characterised by your independent, proactive, and results-oriented work style and your ability to collaborate in cross-functional teams and a demonstrated ability to quickly learn new technology.

At Viatris, we are dedicated to building a truly diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t fully align with every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. You may just be the right candidate for this or other roles.

Benefits at Viatris

At Viatris, we offer competitive salaries, benefits and an inclusive environment where you can use your experiences, perspectives and skills to help make an impact on the lives of others. Some of our benefits include the following on top of a competitive salary:

As a Product Manager, you will help drive growth of direct to consumer revenues for Call of Duty: Mobile, including our own web store and third party stores.   • Experience using SQL, Tableau, Excel, or other analytical tools to generate insights from data

Extra Points

Our World

At Activision, we strive to create the most iconic brands in gaming and entertainment. We’re driven by our mission to deliver unrivaled gaming experiences for the world to enjoy, together. We are home to some of the most beloved entertainment franchises including Call of Duty®, Crash Bandicoot™, Tony Hawk’s™ Pro Skater™, and Guitar Hero®. As a leading worldwide developer, publisher and distributor of interactive entertainment and products, our “press start” is simple: delight hundreds of millions of players around the world with innovative, fun, thrilling, and engaging entertainment experiences.

We’re not just looking back at our decades-long legacy; we’re forging ahead to keep advancing gameplay with some of the most popular titles and sophisticated technology in the world. We have bold ambitions to create the most inclusive company as we know our success comes from the passionate, creative, and diverse teams within our organization.

We’re in the business of delivering fun and unforgettable entertainment for our player community to enjoy. And our future opportunities have never been greater — this could be your opportunity to level up.

Ready to Activate Your Future?

We love hearing from anyone who is enthusiastic about changing the games industry. Not sure you meet all qualifications? Let us decide! Research shows that women and members of other under-represented groups tend to not apply to jobs when they think they may not meet every qualification, when, in fact, they often do! We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment and strongly encourage you to apply.

We are committed to working with and providing reasonable assistance to individuals with physical and mental disabilities. If you are a disabled individual requiring an accommodation to apply for an open position, please email your request to accommodations@activisionblizzard.com. General employment questions cannot be accepted or processed here. Thank you for your interest.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status, among other characteristics.
